selection_reason: No prior evidence exists, so the priority is establishing a strong, interpretable baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest canonical configuration: it uses the most standard RNA encoder (PCA-2000), the simplest profile setting, and avoids confounding from image, aggregation, or fusion choices. This gives a clean reference accuracy for RNA-only performance. In subsequent experiments I can then test image_only (config_010) and multimodal (config_016) with the same PCA-2000 encoder to isolate the marginal contribution of each modality and of fusion, while keeping the RNA representation fixed. Starting from the simplest model avoids the risk of over-crediting complexity and provides the anchor against which all later gains (or losses) are measured—critical when only 10 experiments are available.

The only completed experiment (config_001, RNA-only/PCA/single-profile) yielded a low accuracy of ~48.5%, leaving major uncertainty about whether the image modality provides complementary or superior signal. Testing image_only with a standard pretrained ResNet50 (config_010) isolates the image modality's contribution without confounding from multiprofile, aggregation, or fusion. If image alone achieves comparable or better accuracy, it validates investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion; if it is also poor, it suggests the bottleneck lies in representation quality (motivating scGPT/scVI tests) rather than modality choice. This is the highest-information experiment because it resolves a binary question—does image carry useful signal?—that fundamentally reshapes the search strategy for the remaining 8 experiments.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieved 48.5% accuracy, far outperforming image-only ResNet50 (config_010) at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We have no data on whether multiprofile representation (with aggregation) improves upon the single-profile RNA baseline. This experiment (config_002) makes the minimal change from config_001—switching to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder—thereby isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation on the strongest modality. It is the best next step because it tests a structural axis (single vs. multi-profile) that, if beneficial, would unlock a large family of downstream configurations (better encoders, multimodal fusion) in the remaining 7 experiments, while if neutral or harmful, it rules out an entire design direction early in the budget.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the current best at 0.591 acc, a large jump over singleprofile PCA (0.485), confirming multiprofile is a strong direction. Image-only is very weak (0.208), so the near-term gains likely come from refining the RNA pipeline. Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform avgpool for the same multiprofile PCA setup? config_003 changes only the aggregation (avgpool → transformer) while holding encoder and profile setting fixed, giving a clean single-variable comparison against the current best. Why this is the best use: With 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether transformer aggregation adds value over the simpler avgpool is the highest-information next step. If it helps, it unlocks a family of stronger multimodal configs (e.g., config_020/021); if it doesn't, we avoid wasting budget on transformer-based variants and can pivot to testing learned encoders (scvi/scgpt) or multimodal fusion instead.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the current best at 0.591 acc, and multiprofile+avgpool clearly outperforms both single-profile PCA (0.485) and multiprofile+transformer (0.519). The image modality is very weak (0.208), so RNA encoder quality is the most promising lever. Question: Does replacing PCA with a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) in the proven multiprofile+avgpool setting improve accuracy? This is a clean single-variable change from config_002, isolating the encoder effect. Why best use of budget: With 5 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out encoder improvement in the best-known setting is the highest-information experiment. If scvi_n200 helps, it opens a path to test scgpt and multimodal variants with a stronger RNA backbone; if it doesn't, PCA is validated as sufficient and we can pivot to fusion or image-encoder experiments.

Evidence: The current best is config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. We've established that multiprofile+avgpool is the best profile/aggregation combo, and scvi_n200 beats pca_n2000. The key remaining uncertainty on the RNA side is whether scgpt can outperform scvi_n200. This experiment (config_008: scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool) isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding the proven-best profile and aggregation settings constant. It is the best use of this slot because: (1) it gives a clean single-variable comparison to determine the optimal RNA encoder, (2) the result directly informs whether remaining budget should be spent on multimodal configs with scvi_n200 or scgpt, and (3) with only 4 experiments left after this one, confirming the best RNA backbone before testing multimodal fusion is the most information-efficient path.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.6501 acc. RNA clearly dominates image (0.48-0.65 vs 0.21 for resnet50 image-only), and avgpool beats transformer for aggregation. However, we have not yet tested whether a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l vs the weak resnet50) combined with the best RNA pipeline could push accuracy above 0.65. Question: Does adding image features from a pretrained ViT-L to the already-optimized scvi_n200/multiprofile/avgpool RNA pipeline improve validation accuracy via simple concat fusion? Why this experiment: config_036 isolates the effect of adding a potentially informative image modality to the best RNA configuration, using the simplest fusion (concat) to avoid confounding. It is the highest-potential untested configuration that could beat the current best. If it succeeds, the remaining 3 experiments can refine fusion (weighted) or aggregation (transformer); if it fails, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can spend remaining budget on minor RNA-only variants.

The best result so far is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy. The strongest evidence from RNA-only experiments shows scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool is the optimal RNA pipeline, and adding imagenet_vit_l with concat fusion yields the best overall result. The key untested design choice within this top configuration is the fusion strategy: config_037 is identical to config_036 except it uses weighted fusion instead of concat. This is a clean single-variable comparison that isolates whether learned weighting of modalities improves over simple concatenation. With only 2 experiments remaining, testing this directly exploits the strongest evidence while resolving an important uncertainty about fusion. If weighted fusion matches or beats concat, it informs the final experiment; if not, we confirm concat is optimal and can spend remaining budget on the next most impactful axis (e.g., transformer aggregation in config_038).

The current best is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy. The only untested dimension within this exact model/image/fusion combination is aggregation: config_038 swaps avgpool for transformer while keeping concat fusion. In the RNA-only setting, avgpool clearly outperformed transformer (0.650 vs 0.519), but the multimodal context may change this dynamic—transformer aggregation could capture cross-profile interactions that complement the image features in ways simple averaging cannot. This is a single-variable change from the best config, making it the cleanest exploitation experiment. With only one experiment remaining after this, confirming (or refuting) whether transformer aggregation adds value in the multimodal regime is the highest-information test: if it fails to beat 0.715, we can be confident config_036 is the optimal configuration in the explored space; if it succeeds, we find a new best.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.7207. The evidence strongly supports this family: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder (0.650 RNA-only vs 0.591 pca, 0.530 scgpt), imagenet_vit_l is the best image encoder, multiprofile outperforms single profile, and concat has consistently beaten weighted (0.715 vs 0.706 with avgpool). The only untested configuration in this strongest family is config_039 (transformer + weighted). While weighted has been slightly worse, the small transformer-vs-avgpool gap (0.006) and the possibility of a positive aggregation-fusion interaction mean this is the only remaining configuration with a non-trivial chance of matching or exceeding 0.721. As the final experiment with 0 remaining, completing the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the top family is the highest-expected-value choice, and no other untested configuration (resnet50, scgpt, single profile, RNA-only) has a realistic path to beating the current best.

No experiments have been completed, so the first priority is establishing a clean, interpretable baseline. config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA n2000) is the simplest and most standard configuration in single-cell genomics: PCA is a well-understood linear encoder, single-profile avoids aggregation complexity, and no image modality or fusion is involved. This gives a reference accuracy against which all other RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), profile settings (multiprofile + aggregation), image-only models, and multimodal fusion strategies can be meaningfully compared. Establishing this anchor first reduces uncertainty about the fundamental performance floor and allows subsequent experiments to isolate the incremental contribution of each design choice (better encoder, multiprofile aggregation, image modality, fusion) with 9 remaining experiments.

Evidence: We have one RNA-only baseline (config_001: pca_n2000, singleprofile) at 0.485 accuracy. We have no information about whether image features carry any signal for this task. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) establishes the image-only baseline, which is the second critical reference point needed before evaluating multimodal fusion. Why this is best: Without knowing the image baseline, I cannot judge whether multimodal configurations (configs 016-051) are worthwhile or whether the image modality is simply noisy. This single, clean experiment reduces the largest source of uncertainty in the remaining search space. ResNet50 with singleprofile keeps the comparison simple and directly analogous to the RNA baseline, isolating the effect of modality. With 8 experiments left, establishing both unimodal baselines early allows informed allocation of remaining budget to fusion strategies, encoders, and profile settings.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (ResNet50, single profile) only reaches 0.208, making RNA the dominant modality by a wide margin. Uncertainty: We have no evidence yet on whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can improve upon the simple PCA baseline, and this is the highest-leverage design choice since RNA drives performance. This experiment (config_004) tests scvi_n200 vs PCA n2000 with all other settings held constant (rna_only, singleprofile, no aggregation/fusion), isolating the effect of the RNA representation. It is the best next step because: (1) it is a clean single-variable comparison against config_001, (2) the RNA encoder choice will inform all subsequent multimodal experiments, and (3) with 7 experiments remaining, establishing the best RNA representation early allows informed exploitation in later multimodal and multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: scVI n200 single-profile RNA (config_004, acc 0.5203) is the best result so far, outperforming PCA n2000 (0.4849) and image-only ResNet50 (0.2079). Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether multiprofile aggregation can improve on the best single-profile RNA result. This experiment (config_005: scVI n200, multiprofile, avgpool) directly extends the top-performing configuration by adding the multiprofile dimension with the simplest aggregation (avgpool), isolating the effect of profile aggregation on the best encoder. If multiprofile+avgpool improves accuracy, it justifies further exploration with transformer aggregation and multimodal fusion; if not, we can pivot to scGPT or multimodal directions with the remaining 6 experiments. This is the most informative single step to reduce uncertainty about a key design axis before committing budget to more complex multimodal configurations.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved 0.650 accuracy, the best result so far, showing a large jump over singleprofile scvi_n200 (0.520). Image-only is weak (0.208), so RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool for the multiprofile scvi_n200 setup. This experiment (config_006) tests exactly that—same encoder, same multiprofile setting, only changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer. It is a clean single-variable comparison with the current best, making it the highest-information experiment to either push accuracy above 0.650 or confirm avgpool is sufficient, before spending remaining budget on new encoders (scgpt) or multimodal fusion.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.6530 accuracy. We have strong evidence that multiprofile + scvi_n200 dominates, but scgpt has not been tested at all. Uncertainty: We don't know whether scgpt (a pretrained generative RNA model) could produce a better latent representation than scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting, which would change the optimal encoder for all subsequent experiments. This experiment (config_009: rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) directly compares against config_006 by changing only the RNA encoder, isolating that single variable. Resolving whether scgpt > or < scvi_n200 is critical before spending remaining budget on multimodal fusion experiments, since the choice of RNA encoder will be the backbone of any multimodal configuration. With 4 experiments left, establishing the best RNA encoder first maximizes the value of subsequent multimodal tests.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653. Image-only with resnet50 was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality's contribution is uncertain. The critical open question is whether multimodal fusion can improve upon the strong RNA-only baseline, and whether a stronger image encoder (ViT-L pretrained on ImageNet) changes that picture. This experiment (config_038) takes the exact best RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) and adds imagenet_vit_l with concat fusion, directly testing whether the image modality provides complementary signal when paired with the strongest RNA representation. It is the best use of this slot because: (1) it isolates the effect of adding image to our proven best RNA config, (2) ViT-L is the strongest available image encoder so it gives the image modality its best chance, (3) concat is the simplest fusion, reducing confounds, and (4) the answer determines whether the remaining 3 experiments should explore further multimodal variants or stay in the RNA-only space.

The current best is config_038 (0.7207 acc) using scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + concat. The only untested dimension within this exact configuration family is the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted). Config_039 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, isolating that single variable. RNA-only evidence (transformer ≈ avgpool) suggests aggregation is not the bottleneck, making fusion the most promising untested lever.

The current best (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The only untested variation that isolates a single design choice from this best configuration is config_037, which swaps transformer for avgpool aggregation while keeping all other settings identical. In the RNA-only multiprofile setting, transformer and avgpool were nearly equivalent (0.653 vs 0.650), so it is uncertain whether transformer's marginal edge persists in the multimodal regime where image features are high-dimensional and pre-structured. Testing config_037 clarifies whether aggregation type is a meaningful lever in the multimodal setting. If it matches or beats 0.725, we confirm a new best; if it is worse, it validates transformer as the correct aggregation and gives us high confidence that config_039 is near the ceiling for this architecture family, allowing the final experiment to be directed at the most remaining uncertainty. This is the cleanest single-variable comparison available and the best use of experiment 9 with only 1 slot remaining.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). All four scvi_n200+ViT multiprofile aggregation/fusion combinations are now tested, confirming transformer+weighted as optimal for that RNA encoder. The one remaining uncertainty at the top of the performance range is whether the RNA encoder choice still matters when paired with the strongest image encoder (ViT-L). config_027 isolates exactly this: it is identical to config_039 except PCA_n2000 replaces scvi_n200. In RNA-only settings, scvi_n200 beat PCA by ~0.035 (single) and likely more (multiprofile), but in a multimodal regime where the ViT provides a strong learned representation, a 2000-dim linear PCA might capture complementary variance that the 200-dim scvi bottleneck discards. This is the cleanest remaining A/B comparison, requires changing only one factor, and directly tests whether the best configuration found so far is truly optimal or whether a different RNA representation could push accuracy higher. As the final experiment, it either confirms config_039 as the winner or reveals a surprise, maximizing information under zero remaining budget.

With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is establishing a performance floor. Config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-2000) is the simplest, most standard baseline in the design space. It tests how much signal RNA alone provides with a straightforward linear dimensionality reduction, giving a reference point against which to measure the incremental value of (a) image modality, (b) learned RNA encoders (scvi, scGPT), (c) multiprofile aggregation, and (d) multimodal fusion. Establishing this floor first ensures that in the remaining 9 experiments I can make informed exploitation/exploration trade-offs rather than assuming complexity will help. It is also the lowest-cost configuration to run, allowing a quick readout to guide the next step.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: RNA-only, PCA, single-profile at ~48.5% acc), the highest-uncertainty question is whether the image modality carries useful signal for this task. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the simplest image-only baseline and directly answers this. Under a 10-experiment budget, resolving the modality question early is the most information-dense use of experiment 2.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieved 0.485 accuracy while image (ResNet50) was very weak at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant signal. Evidence: scvi_n200 singleprofile (config_004, acc=0.520) is the best result so far, clearly outperforming pca_n2000 singleprofile (0.485) and image-only resnet50 (0.208). The dominant signal is RNA, and the scvi encoder is the strongest RNA representation tested. Uncertainty: We have no evidence yet on whether multiprofile aggregation adds value over singleprofile. This experiment tests exactly that: it extends the best configuration (scvi_n200) to multiprofile with a simple avgpool aggregation, isolating the profile-setting effect while keeping the encoder fixed. If multiprofile+avgpool improves over 0.520, it justifies further investment in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, multimodal fusion). If it does not, we can redirect remaining budget toward scgpt or multimodal exploration. This is the highest-information single-variable step under the remaining 6-experiment budget.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over the singleprofile baseline (0.520). The key open question is whether the aggregation method can be improved: transformer aggregation could capture richer inter-profile relationships compared to simple avgpool. config_006 is a clean single-variable comparison (avgpool → transformer) holding all else constant (scvi_n200, multiprofile, rna_only), directly isolating the aggregation effect on the best-performing setup. This is the highest-value next step because: (1) it exploits the strongest evidence by testing a logical extension, (2) the answer will determine whether transformer aggregation is worth pursuing in the remaining multimodal configurations, and (3) with 5 experiments left, confirming or ruling out the aggregation upgrade early lets the remaining budget focus on encoder choice or multimodal fusion with confidence.

Evidence: Multiprofile with scvi_n200 is the clear winner so far (0.650-0.653), far exceeding singleprofile RNA (0.485-0.520) and image-only (0.208). Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting, or is scvi_n200 already near-optimal for RNA representation? If scgpt multiprofile matches or beats 0.653, it opens a new exploitation path; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 and can pivot remaining budget to multimodal fusion with confidence.

Evidence: RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 + transformer (config_006, acc=0.653) is the current best, and multiprofile + scvi_n200 is clearly the strongest RNA setup. Image-only with resnet50 was very weak (0.208), but we have not yet tested the stronger imagenet_vit_l encoder. This experiment (config_038) takes the best RNA configuration (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) and adds imagenet_vit_l with concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion can exceed 0.653. It is the highest-value test because: (1) it isolates the effect of adding a strong image modality to the proven-best RNA pipeline, (2) concat is the simpler fusion choice reducing confounds, and (3) with only 3 experiments remaining, we need to determine early whether the multimodal direction is viable or whether we should focus remaining budget on RNA-only refinements.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.7207 accuracy. The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. The completed experiments have tested 3 of the 4 cells in the aggregation×fusion grid for this top multimodal family: transformer+concat (0.7207), transformer+weighted (0.7250), and avgpool+weighted (0.7062). With no prior evidence, the most important first step is to establish a clean, minimal baseline that isolates the RNA signal without confounding factors from image modality, complex encoders, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: a linear PCA reduction of the RNA profile with no additional architectural complexity. This gives a reference accuracy/F1 against which all subsequent experiments (stronger RNA encoders like scvi/scgpt, image-only models, multimodal fusion, multiprofile aggregation) can be meaningfully compared. Establishing this floor first reduces uncertainty about whether the task is solvable at all and how much headroom more complex designs might offer, making the remaining 9 experiments far more informative.

The sole completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) yielded a very low validation accuracy of 48.5%, establishing a weak RNA-only baseline. With 8 experiments remaining, the most critical unknown is whether the image modality carries stronger signal than RNA for this task. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is a clean, single-variable comparison against config_001: it changes only the modality while keeping the profile setting (singleprofile) and architectural simplicity (no aggregation/fusion) identical. If image accuracy substantially exceeds 48.5%, the remaining budget should pivot toward image-centric or multimodal configurations; if it is comparable or lower, RNA improvements (better encoders, multiprofile) or multimodal fusion become the priority. This modality-level comparison is the highest-information experiment to guide the rest of the search and avoids committing to a specific encoder or fusion strategy before knowing which modality is most informative.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA n2000) achieves 48.5% accuracy, far outperforming config_010 (image-only, ResNet50) at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) improves over the linear PCA baseline, which is a fundamental representation choice. This experiment (config_004) isolates exactly that variable: same model setting (RNA-only), same profile setting (single-profile), same architecture, but swapping PCA n2000 for scvi_n200. If scvi_n200 matches or beats PCA, it signals that learned nonlinear representations add value and justifies further investment in advanced encoders (scgpt) and multimodal fusion with better RNA features. If PCA remains superior, it tells us the signal is largely linear and we should focus budget on profile/aggregation or fusion strategies rather than encoder complexity. This is the cleanest single-variable comparison available and the highest-information experiment before committing to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: scVI n200 (0.520 acc) outperforms PCA n2000 (0.485 acc) as the RNA encoder, and image-only is very weak (0.208 acc). The best single-profile RNA result is 0.520. Uncertainty: We have no data on whether multiprofile + aggregation improves RNA performance, which is a fundamental design axis. This experiment (config_005) tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation using the best encoder (scVI n200), isolating the profile/aggregation effect with a minimal, interpretable change from config_004. Choosing avgpool over transformer keeps the comparison conservative and reduces overfitting risk. If multiprofile+avgpool lifts accuracy meaningfully over 0.520, it validates the multiprofile axis and justifies further exploration (transformer, multimodal multiprofile). If it does not, we save budget by ruling out that direction before committing to more complex multimodal variants. This is the highest-information single step given 6 remaining experiments.

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc, showing that multiprofile + scvi_n200 is a strong direction. The key remaining uncertainty within this promising branch is whether transformer aggregation outperforms simple avgpool for combining multiple profiles. Config_006 isolates exactly this variable (aggregation: avgpool → transformer) while holding encoder (scvi_n200), profile setting (multiprofile), and modality (RNA-only) constant. This is the cleanest single-variable extension of the current best, and with 5 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out the aggregation upgrade before branching into new encoders (scgpt) or multimodal fusion is the most efficient use of the next slot.

Evidence: scvi_n200 with multiprofile+transformer is the current best (0.653), and multiprofile is the dominant driver of performance. However, we have no data on scgpt in the multiprofile setting, leaving uncertainty about whether a pretrained generative RNA encoder could outperform scvi_n200. This experiment (config_009: rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) changes only the RNA encoder relative to config_006, cleanly isolating the encoder effect. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a stronger base for multimodal fusion in remaining experiments; if it underperforms, we confirm scvi_n200 as the best encoder and can confidently allocate remaining budget to multimodal fusion with the proven encoder. With 4 experiments left, resolving the encoder question now is the highest-value uncertainty reduction before committing to more complex multimodal configurations.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. The image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.208), but that used a relatively weak encoder. The key untested question is whether adding the strongest available image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) to the best RNA configuration via multimodal fusion can push past 0.653. Config_038 directly extends config_006 by adding ViT-L image features with the same multiprofile + transformer aggregation and a standard concat fusion, isolating the effect of adding image information. With only 3 experiments remaining, this is the highest-value test: if it succeeds, we find a new best; if it fails, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can spend remaining budget fine-tuning RNA-only settings (e.g., testing whether scgpt+avgpool or other small variations help). Testing a weaker image encoder (resnet50) in multimodal mode would be less informative given its already-terrible standalone performance.

The current best result is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy, which substantially outperforms the RNA-only multiprofile baseline (0.653). The image modality alone was weak (0.208 with resnet50), but the ViT-L encoder in the multimodal setting clearly adds value. The key remaining question within this winning configuration is whether the fusion strategy can be improved: concat treats both modalities equally, while weighted fusion could allow the model to adaptively downweight the weaker image signal and upweight the stronger RNA signal. Config_039 isolates exactly one variable (fusion: concat→weighted) from the current best, making it a clean exploitation experiment. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, testing the most promising single modification to the current champion is the highest-value use of the next slot, and the result will directly inform whether the final 2 experiments should further refine this configuration or explore an alternative.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder, multiprofile, and weighted fusion. The one remaining untested variation within this optimal multimodal setup is the aggregation method: avgpool vs. transformer. In RNA-only, transformer (0.653) narrowly beat avgpool (0.650), and in multimodal, weighted (0.725) narrowly beat concat (0.721). Testing config_037 (avgpool + weighted) isolates the aggregation effect while holding all other settings at their best values. If it performs comparably to config_039, it confirms we are at a performance plateau and config_039 is near-optimal; if it outperforms, we find a new best. This is the cleanest single-variable comparison remaining and the most informative use of experiment 9, leaving experiment 10 for a final confirmation or minor refinement.

The current best is config_039 (0.7250) with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + weighted. All four aggregation×fusion combinations for this exact model setting are now tested, confirming transformer+weighted is optimal. The key remaining uncertainty is how much the image encoder quality contributes in the multimodal setting: resnet50 alone scored only 0.208, yet imagenet_vit_l in multimodal adds ~7% over RNA-only. Config_033 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted) isolates the image-encoder effect while holding all other parameters at their best-known values, making it the cleanest single-variable comparison to config_039. It is the highest-expected-performance untested configuration given that scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, and weighted are all confirmed as the best settings for their respective axes. As the final experiment, it either confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential to the 0.7250 result or reveals that the RNA encoder dominates, either way maximizing our understanding of the best achievable accuracy within budget.

With no prior evidence, the highest-value first experiment is to establish the simplest, most interpretable baseline: RNA-only with a single profile and PCA (n=2000) encoding. This configuration has no aggregation, fusion, or image components, so its validation accuracy provides a clean reference point against which every subsequent design choice (image modality, learned encoders like scVI/scGPT, multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion) can be measured. Knowing the RNA-PCA single-profile accuracy first lets me (a) determine whether adding an image modality or a more complex RNA encoder actually improves performance, (b) calibrate how much headroom exists for the remaining 9 experiments, and (c) avoid over-investing in complex multimodal or multiprofile variants if the simple baseline is already strong. It is the single experiment that reduces the most uncertainty about the entire search space.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA → 48.5% acc), evidence is extremely sparse. The most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries comparable or complementary signal to RNA. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest direct counterpart to config_001, swapping only the modality while keeping profile setting and simplicity level identical. This isolates the modality effect and tells us whether image features are informative at all, which determines whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing in later experiments. Under a 10-experiment budget, establishing the relative value of each modality early is essential before investing in more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: RNA (PCA, single profile) achieves 48.5% accuracy while image (ResNet50) is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant signal. PCA is a simple linear projection and likely underperforms learned encoders on single-cell data. Question: Does replacing PCA with a learned variational encoder (scvi_n200) improve RNA representation quality and validation accuracy? This experiment changes only the RNA encoder while keeping single-profile and no aggregation fixed, cleanly isolating the encoder effect. If scvi substantially improves over 48.5%, it justifies investing remaining budget in scvi-based multimodal or multiprofile configurations; if not, PCA is sufficient and we should pivot to aggregation/fusion strategies. This is a minimal, single-variable change from the best-performing config so far.

Evidence: RNA-only with scvi_n200 (config_004, acc=0.5203) is the best result so far, clearly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.4849) and image-only (0.2079). This confirms scvi_n200 as the preferred RNA encoder. Uncertainty: multiprofile with aggregation is completely untested and could capture complementary information across profiles. Question: Does moving from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improve on the best RNA-only result while keeping the proven scvi_n200 encoder? Why this experiment: config_005 is the minimal, logical extension of config_004 (changing only profile_setting and adding aggregation), isolating the multiprofile+aggregation effect. Choosing avgpool over transformer first is the simpler baseline; if it helps, transformer becomes a natural follow-up. With 6 experiments remaining after this, this single-variable change maximizes information gain about whether multiprofile is a productive direction before committing budget to more complex multimodal or scgpt variants.

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation with scvi_n200 is a strong direction. The key uncertainty is whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) can further improve over simple avgpool for the multiprofile setting. Config_006 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the best encoder (scvi_n200) and multiprofile setting, isolating the aggregation effect. This is the cleanest single-variable extension of the current best result, and resolving whether transformer aggregation helps will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based multimodal configs or focus on other axes (encoder, fusion). With 5 experiments left, this high-value comparison is the best use of the next slot.

Evidence: The multiprofile setting with scvi_n200 is the clear winner so far (0.650-0.653), with transformer aggregation marginally ahead of avgpool (0.653 vs 0.650). Image-only models are weak (0.208), and singleprofile RNA tops out around 0.52. Uncertainty: We have not tested the scgpt encoder, a pretrained foundation model, in the multiprofile setting. It could potentially outperform scvi_n200 by leveraging richer pretraining. This experiment (config_009: scgpt, multiprofile, transformer) directly isolates the encoder effect by holding aggregation (transformer) and profile setting (multiprofile) constant relative to the current best (config_006). If scgpt improves on 0.653, we identify a stronger RNA backbone to build multimodal fusion on in remaining experiments. If it does not, we confirm scvi_n200 as the best encoder and can confidently direct remaining budget toward multimodal fusion strategies. This is the highest-information experiment: it tests the single most impactful untested variable (encoder) in the most promising architectural setting.

The best result so far is config_006 (RNA-only, multi-profile, scVI n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc, and the RNA-only space appears well-characterized (scVI n200 >> PCA/scGPT; multi-profile >> single-profile; transformer ≈ avgpool). The key unexplored question is whether adding the image modality to this already-optimized RNA pipeline yields complementary signal or merely dilutes it, given that image-only ResNet50 scored only 0.208. Config_032 (multimodal, multi-profile, scVI n200, ResNet50, transformer, concat) is the most direct and minimal extension of config_006: it changes only the model setting from RNA-only to multimodal with the simplest fusion (concat), isolating the effect of adding image. If concat fusion helps, a follow-up with weighted fusion (config_033) could further tune the balance; if it hurts, we confirm the RNA signal is self-sufficient and can spend remaining budget on other refinements. With 3 experiments left, this single test gives the highest information gain about whether the multimodal direction is worth further investment.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688. The image-only baseline with resnet50 was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image contribution in config_032 may be limited by the encoder's representational capacity. Config_038 changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings identical (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, concat), cleanly isolating the effect of image representation quality. This is the best use of experiment 8 because: (1) it directly extends the strongest configuration with a single-variable change, (2) it tests whether the modest 3.5% multimodal gain can be amplified by a stronger visual encoder, and (3) if it succeeds, the remaining 2 experiments can further optimize fusion or aggregation around the improved image backbone; if it fails, we confirm the image signal is inherently weak and can focus remaining budget on RNA-side refinements.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.7207 accuracy. All other design dimensions (RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, aggregation) have been well-characterized and point to this configuration. The only untested variable in this top-performing setup is the fusion strategy: we have only tested concat, never weighted. config_039 is the exact same configuration as config_038 but with weighted fusion instead of concat—a clean single-variable comparison. This is the highest-value experiment because it directly tests whether a learned or adaptive fusion can improve on the current best, and with only 1 experiment remaining after this, exploiting the strongest known direction with a minimal change maximizes the probability of finding a new best.

The best result so far is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. In the RNA-only multiprofile setting, transformer (0.653) and avgpool (0.650) aggregation were nearly identical, suggesting the aggregation choice may interact differently when combined with multimodal weighted fusion. Config_037 makes the single minimal change of swapping transformer for avgpool while retaining all other best-performing components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, weighted fusion). This isolates the aggregation effect in the multimodal weighted-fusion regime, where the interaction between profile aggregation and cross-modal fusion weights could shift the balance. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability test to either marginally exceed 0.725 or confirm transformer as the optimal aggregation, while avoiding the low-probability alternatives (scgpt or PCA encoders, which were substantially weaker in RNA-only).

With no prior evidence, the highest-priority uncertainty is establishing a reliable performance baseline for the most fundamental modality. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest, most standard RNA baseline: PCA is a fast, well-understood linear encoder unlikely to introduce confounding failure modes, and singleprofile avoids the additional complexity of aggregation. This experiment isolates the RNA signal quality without any confounding from image data, learned encoders, or multi-profile aggregation. It gives a clean reference point against which all subsequent experiments (image baseline, learned RNA encoders, multimodal fusion) can be compared. Starting with the simplest viable model before adding complexity is the most budget-efficient way to reduce uncertainty in experiment 1 of 10.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality provides any useful signal for this task. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) directly tests this by isolating the image contribution while keeping the profile setting (singleprofile) identical to config_001, so the comparison cleanly separates the effect of modality. If image-only accuracy is competitive or complementary to the RNA baseline, it justifies investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion configs; if it is poor, we can focus on improving the RNA side (better encoders, multiprofile aggregation). This single experiment resolves the highest-level architectural question before committing to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations, making it the best use of experiment 2 under the 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy, clearly outperforming image (ResNet50) at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether leveraging multiple profiles with simple aggregation (avgpool) can improve upon the single-profile RNA baseline. It is the best next step because it is a minimal, single-variable extension of the current best result, will tell us whether multiprofile is a productive direction before investing in more complex aggregations (transformer) or alternative encoders (scvi, scgpt), and preserves budget for follow-up experiments if multiprofile proves beneficial.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a substantial +10.6% gain over config_001 (singleprofile, 0.485), confirming that multiprofile aggregation is the most impactful design choice so far. Image-only is weak (0.208), so RNA-centric exploration is the priority. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether transformer aggregation (which models inter-profile interactions) outperforms simple average pooling. This experiment (config_003) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding encoder (pca_n2000), profile setting (multiprofile), and modality (rna_only) fixed, giving a clean single-variable comparison against config_002. Why this is the best next step: With 6 experiments remaining, isolating the aggregation effect is the highest-information experiment because the result directly determines whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based multimodal configs (configs 020/021/026/027 etc.) or to focus on encoder upgrades (scvi, scgpt) with avgpool. It is a low-risk, high-information exploitation of the current best direction.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the current best at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile+avgpool is the strongest RNA configuration tested. Image alone is very weak (0.208), so the RNA encoder is the most impactful design axis to explore next. Question: Does replacing PCA with a learned latent encoder (scvi_n200) improve accuracy in the same multiprofile+avgpool setup? This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_002, isolating the effect of the RNA representation. Why: With 5 experiments remaining, establishing the best RNA encoder before moving to multimodal fusion is critical—any multimodal model built on a suboptimal RNA backbone will be limited. If scvi_n200 improves over PCA, we gain a stronger foundation for the remaining experiments; if not, PCA remains our best bet and we can pivot to multimodal testing with confidence.

The current best is config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.6501 accuracy. The strongest evidence shows that learned encoders (scvi_n200) outperform PCA, and avgpool beats transformer for aggregation. The key remaining uncertainty in the RNA-only space is whether scgpt, another learned encoder, can match or exceed scvi_n200 under identical conditions. Config_008 (scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool) isolates exactly this encoder comparison while holding aggregation and profile setting constant. This is the best use of experiment 6 because: (1) it is a clean single-variable comparison that reduces uncertainty about which encoder to build upon, (2) if scgpt is superior, we gain a new best direction to exploit in the remaining 4 experiments (e.g., multimodal scgpt), and (3) if scgpt is inferior, we confirm scvi_n200 as the optimal encoder and can confidently pivot to testing whether multimodal fusion with the best RNA encoder adds value. This avoids the risk of jumping to multimodal (where image alone was very weak at 0.21) before fully characterizing the RNA encoder landscape.

Evidence: The best RNA-only configuration is scVI_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool (config_005, acc 0.650), clearly outperforming PCA (0.591) and scGPT (0.530) under the same setup. Image-only with ResNet50 is very weak (0.208), raising the question of whether image features add any complementary signal in a multimodal setting. Uncertainty: It is unknown whether fusing image features with the strong scVI_n200 RNA representation helps or hurts performance. This experiment (config_030: multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_n200, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) directly tests whether adding the image modality to the best RNA configuration provides a benefit, using the simplest fusion (concat) and the aggregation (avgpool) already shown to be superior to transformer. This is the best use of the next slot because: (1) it isolates the effect of adding image features to the current best model, (2) if it helps, the remaining 3 experiments can optimize the multimodal setup (e.g., try ViT-L or weighted fusion); if it does not help, the remaining budget can focus on RNA-only refinements, and (3) it changes only one design dimension (adding image + fusion) relative to the proven best RNA config, keeping the comparison clean.

The current best is config_005 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650. The multimodal counterpart config_030 (same settings + resnet50, concat fusion) scored only 0.632, suggesting the image modality is adding noise under simple concatenation. Config_031 changes only the fusion strategy (concat → weighted) while holding all other factors constant (scvi_n200, multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool), directly testing whether learned weighting can downweight the weak image signal and allow the multimodal model to match or exceed the RNA-only baseline. This is the cleanest single-variable comparison available to determine whether multimodal fusion has any rescue path with the best RNA encoder. With 2 experiments remaining, resolving this question is critical: if weighted fusion recovers the gap, a multimodal config becomes competitive; if not, we can confidently commit remaining budget to RNA-only refinements. It is preferable to config_006 (scvi+transformer) because two data points already show avgpool > transformer, making that test lower-value.

The current best is config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.678 accuracy. The evidence shows that (1) scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder, (2) avgpool outperforms transformer aggregation, (3) weighted fusion beats concat, and (4) adding image with weighted fusion gives a modest boost over RNA-only (0.678 vs 0.650). The image modality contributed ~0.028 improvement with resnet50, but image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.21), suggesting the image encoder quality is a bottleneck. config_037 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a substantially stronger pretrained backbone), keeping all other settings identical to the current best. This is a clean single-variable test that isolates whether a stronger image representation can further improve the weighted multimodal fusion. With only 1 experiment remaining, exploiting the proven best configuration while testing the most impactful unexplored variable (image encoder strength) is the highest-value use of the final budget slot.

The current best is config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.7062. All major design axes have been explored: scvi_n200 > pca > scgpt, multiprofile > singleprofile, weighted > concat, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, and avgpool > transformer (in RNA-only). The one remaining untested perturbation of the current best is replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping everything else identical (config_039). Although avgpool outperformed transformer in RNA-only settings, the multimodal context introduces cross-modal interactions across profiles that a transformer might capture more effectively than simple averaging. This is a clean single-variable comparison against the current best. As the final experiment, it either yields a new best (if transformer benefits from multimodal profile interactions) or definitively confirms config_037 as the optimal configuration found within budget.

No prior evidence exists, so the first experiment should establish a simple, interpretable baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal RNA configuration: a standard linear dimensionality reduction on a single profile with no aggregation or fusion complexity. Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only ~48.5% validation accuracy, a weak baseline that gives little signal about which design axis (modality, encoder, aggregation, fusion) will drive improvement. Uncertainty: The most critical open question is whether the image modality carries substantially more discriminative information than the RNA profile for this task. This experiment tests image_only with a strong pretrained encoder (resnet50) at the same singleprofile setting, providing a clean modality-level comparison against config_001. If image_only substantially outperforms 48.5%, it strongly justifies investing remaining budget in multimodal configurations; if it is comparable or worse, it signals that the bottleneck is representation quality (encoder choice) rather than modality, redirecting effort toward scvi/scgpt encoders. This is the highest-information single experiment at this stage because the modality decision gates the architecture of all subsequent multimodal experiments (configs 016-051) and determines where to focus the remaining 8 experiments.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is very weak at 20.8%, indicating RNA is the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether the PCA representation is already near-optimal for RNA or whether a learned encoder (scVI) can extract more discriminative signal. If it does not, PCA is sufficient and we can pivot to exploring multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments remaining, establishing the best RNA representation early is critical because it underpins all multimodal configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (0.5203 acc, config_004), outperforming pca_n2000 (0.4849, config_001), while image-only is very weak (0.2079). The current best result is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.6501 accuracy, showing a large gain over single-profile (0.5203). The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. The key open question is whether adding the image modality can improve upon this strong RNA-only baseline. Image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), suggesting limited standalone value, but it may still provide complementary signal in a fused setting. Evidence: The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653.
