Image-only is very weak (0.208), making multimodal gains uncertain. Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder in the multiprofile + transformer pipeline? This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_006, isolating encoder quality. Why this is best: With 4 experiments left, we need to determine whether the RNA encoder is the bottleneck before investing budget in multimodal fusion. If scgpt improves on 0.653, it gives a stronger baseline for subsequent multimodal tests; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 is optimal and can focus remaining experiments on whether multimodal (especially with ViT-L) adds value over the RNA-only ceiling.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. RNA is clearly dominant (0.48–0.65) while image alone is weak (0.21 with resnet50). scvi_n200 + multiprofile is the strongest RNA setup, and transformer ≈ avgpool (0.653 vs 0.650). Key uncertainty: whether adding image features to this strong RNA baseline provides complementary signal that improves accuracy, or whether the weak image (0.21) dilutes the RNA signal. This experiment (config_032) directly extends the best RNA-only result by adding resnet50 image features via concat fusion in the multiprofile+transformer setting, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It is the most logical single-step exploitation of our strongest evidence. With 3 experiments remaining after this, a positive result would justify further multimodal exploration; a null/negative result would confirm RNA-only multiprofile as the ceiling and allow the remaining budget to focus on RNA-side refinements.

The best result so far is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The image modality was very weak in isolation (resnet50: 0.208), yet adding it to the strong RNA pipeline gave a ~3.5% boost, suggesting the image contribution is real but may be limited by encoder quality. Config_038 is a single-variable change from config_032: swapping resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings identical (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, concat fusion). This isolates the effect of image encoder capacity on multimodal performance. It is the highest-uncertainty axis remaining: if ViT-L unlocks substantially more image signal, we could see a meaningful jump beyond 0.688; if not, we confirm the image contribution is encoder-agnostic and can focus remaining budget on fusion. With 2 experiments left, this controlled comparison is the most informative use of the next slot.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy. The only untested dimension within this exact configuration family is the fusion strategy (weighted vs. concat). Given the large asymmetry between modalities (RNA-only multiprofile ~0.65 vs. image-only ~0.21), a weighted fusion could potentially rebalance the contribution of each modality and improve over simple concatenation. This experiment isolates a single variable (fusion method) from the best-known configuration, making it the highest-value test: if weighted fusion helps, we find a new best; if not, we confirm concat is optimal and can use the final experiment to explore other directions (e.g., avgpool aggregation). With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the most direct extension of the current best is the most efficient use of budget.

The best result so far is config_039 (0.7250): multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted. The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 over scgpt/PCA, imagenet_vit_l over resnet50, and multiprofile over singleprofile. The only untested variation within this winning family is the aggregation method (avgpool vs transformer). Config_037 tests whether the weighted-fusion advantage observed with transformer aggregation (0.7250 vs 0.7207 for concat) also holds with avgpool, isolating the aggregation effect while keeping the best fusion strategy fixed. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability configuration to approach or marginally exceed the current best, and it provides a clean ablation of aggregation robustness for the top-performing pipeline.

With no prior evidence, the most critical first step is to establish the simplest possible baseline to anchor all future comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal configuration in the space: a single RNA profile encoded with PCA (a fast, interpretable linear method). This tells us (1) whether RNA data alone carries sufficient signal for the task, (2) the performance floor against which more complex encoders (scvi, scgpt), multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion must be judged, and (3) whether the task is solvable from a single modality at all. Establishing this floor first ensures that subsequent experiments—testing image-only, multimodal, or more sophisticated encoders—can be interpreted against a known reference rather than in a vacuum. Under a 10-experiment budget, spending one slot on the simplest baseline is the highest-information-per-experiment choice before exploring the richer design space.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the dominant uncertainty is whether the image modality is informative at all and whether it could complement or outperform RNA. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides the cleanest direct comparison: same profile setting (single), a standard pretrained encoder (ResNet-50), isolating the modality effect. If image accuracy is comparable or better than RNA, multimodal fusion becomes a promising direction to exploit in later experiments. If image is substantially worse, we can focus remaining budget on improving RNA representations (scvi, scgpt) and aggregation. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty with minimal confounding, making it the highest-information choice for experiment 2 of 10.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 single profile (config_001) achieved 0.485 accuracy, far outperforming image-only ResNet50 (config_010, 0.208), establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether multiprofile aggregation can further improve the RNA signal, or whether the single-profile PCA representation is already near its ceiling. This experiment (config_002) tests the minimal extension of the best config by adding multiprofile + avgpool aggregation while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder, isolating the effect of profile aggregation. It is the best use of experiment 3 because it directly exploits the strongest signal found so far, changes only one design axis (profile/aggregation), and will tell us whether to invest remaining budget in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, better encoders) or pivot toward encoder quality and multimodal fusion.

Evidence: RNA multiprofile with avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) substantially outperforms RNA singleprofile (config_001, acc=0.485), while image-only (config_010, acc=0.208) is very weak. This confirms multiprofile RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for multiprofile RNA. This experiment (config_003) directly compares transformer vs. avgpool aggregation while holding all other factors constant (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000), isolating the aggregation effect. This is the best next step because it is a clean, single-variable comparison in the most promising region, and the result will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based aggregation for downstream multimodal or encoder experiments.

Evidence: RNA dominates (0.485-0.591 vs 0.208 for image), and the best config so far is rna_only/multiprofile/pca_n2000/avgpool at 0.591. Multiprofile+avgpool clearly outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation. Question: Can a more expressive RNA encoder (scgpt, a pretrained single-cell foundation model) improve on PCA's linear projection while keeping the proven multiprofile+avgpool pipeline? This isolates the encoder effect with all other settings held at their best-known values. Why this is the best use of experiment 5: It directly tests whether the current 0.591 ceiling is due to PCA's limitations or is a fundamental limit of the RNA-only pipeline, which determines whether to invest remaining budget in better encoders or pivot to multimodal fusion. With 5 experiments left, establishing the RNA encoder ceiling before adding fusion complexity is the most informative next step.

The best result so far is config_002 (RNA-only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 accuracy. Image alone is very weak (0.208), but it may carry complementary information not captured by RNA. The critical open question is whether multimodal fusion can surpass the best RNA-only baseline. Config_018 directly extends config_002 by adding the resnet50 image branch with the same multiprofile/avgpool settings and simple concat fusion, isolating the effect of fusion without changing any other design choice. If it beats 0.591, the remaining 4 experiments can exploit the multimodal direction (e.g., try weighted fusion, ViT encoder, or better RNA encoders). If it does not, we can confidently focus remaining budget on RNA-only refinements (e.g., scvi_n200 with multiprofile/avgpool). This is the highest-information experiment because it determines which branch of the search space to commit the remaining budget to.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc. The image-only baseline is very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality contributes limited signal and may be better served by a learned weighting rather than a fixed concatenation. config_019 is a clean single-variable comparison to config_018, isolating fusion strategy (weighted vs concat) while holding all other settings constant. This directly tests whether the model can learn to down-weight the weaker image branch and up-weight the stronger RNA branch, which is the most impactful architectural question given the large modality imbalance. With 3 experiments remaining, resolving the fusion question now allows the next two to either exploit the better fusion with a stronger image encoder (ViT) or confirm the current best, making this the highest-information-use experiment under the budget.

The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.639). The image modality alone is weak (ResNet50: 0.208), yet it still adds ~5% over RNA-only in the multimodal setting, suggesting the image features contribute useful complementary signal. The most natural single-variable extension is to upgrade the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L while keeping everything else identical (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of image representation quality. If ViT-L provides richer spatial/texture features, it should push accuracy above 0.639; if not, it confirms the bottleneck is elsewhere. With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-value exploitation of the current best direction, and it avoids the transformer aggregation which was clearly inferior to avgpool in all RNA-only comparisons (0.519 vs 0.591).

The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6390 accuracy. The strongest evidence shows weighted fusion > concat, avgpool > transformer, multiprofile > singleprofile, and pca_n2000 > scgpt in RNA-only. However, scvi_n200 has never been tested in any experiment. Config_031 is a single-variable change from the current best (swapping pca_n2000 → scvi_n200 while keeping all other proven-optimal settings: resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile). This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder in the multimodal context and tests whether a learned variational representation can capture complementary biological signal that PCA misses. It is the best use of this experiment because it directly challenges the current best with a minimal, well-motivated perturbation; if it succeeds it pushes past 0.6390, and if it fails we retain config_019 as the top result with one experiment remaining for a final refinement.

The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6776. The evidence shows scvi_n200 is a strong RNA encoder (0.678 vs 0.639 for pca_n2000 in the same multimodal setting), avgpool outperforms transformer, and weighted fusion beats concat. The one untested dimension on top of config_031 is the image encoder: in the pca_n2000 setting, resnet50 (0.639) and imagenet_vit_l (0.635) were close, but with the stronger scvi_n200 RNA representation the interaction with a higher-capacity image encoder (ViT-L) may shift. config_037 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l, isolating that effect. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability single-variable extension to potentially exceed 0.678, while avoiding the clearly inferior transformer aggregation or the weaker scgpt encoder.

With no prior evidence, the most critical first step is to establish the simplest possible baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the minimal configuration: single modality, single profile, linear dimensionality reduction, no aggregation or fusion. This tells us whether the RNA signal alone carries sufficient information for the task and provides a performance floor. If it performs well, it raises the bar that more complex multimodal or learned-encoder models must clear; if it underperforms, it motivates exploring learned encoders (scvi, scgpt) or adding the image modality. Choosing the simplest baseline first avoids conflating multiple design choices and gives the cleanest reference point for the remaining 9 experiments.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved 48.5% accuracy, establishing a modest RNA-only baseline. The single most important structural question is whether the image modality carries complementary or superior signal, since this determines whether the remaining 8 experiments should focus on multimodal fusion or on refining RNA-only representations. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides a clean single-modality comparison to config_001—same profile setting, same architectural simplicity, only the modality and encoder differ. If image-only substantially outperforms 48.5%, image is highly informative and multimodal configs become the priority; if it is comparable or worse, RNA improvements (learned encoders, multiprofile) may be more productive. Why this is the best next step: it isolates the modality question with minimal confounding (no fusion, no aggregation), reduces the largest source of uncertainty in the design space, and directly informs allocation of the remaining 8 experiments across the multimodal vs. single-modality branches.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while Image (ResNet50, single profile) achieves only 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether using multiple profiles with aggregation (avgpool) improves upon the single-profile RNA baseline. This experiment (config_002) isolates the effect of multiprofile + avgpool aggregation while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder as config_001, making it a clean single-variable comparison. It is the best next step because it tests a fundamental architectural choice (single vs. multiprofile) for the clearly dominant modality; if multiprofile helps, it validates the aggregation pathway and justifies investing remaining budget in transformer aggregation and multimodal multiprofile variants, while if it doesn't help, it eliminates ~15 configurations and redirects budget toward encoder improvements (scvi/scgpt) or better image encoders (ViT-L).

Evidence: Multiprofile with avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) substantially outperforms singleprofile (config_001, acc=0.485), confirming that aggregating multiple profiles is highly beneficial for the RNA modality. Image-only models are weak (0.208), so RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether transformer aggregation would further improve over avgpool for the multiprofile RNA setting. This experiment (config_003) isolates exactly one variable—aggregation method (transformer vs. avgpool)—while holding model_setting=rna_only, profile_setting=multiprofile, and rna_encoder=pca_n2000 fixed, matching the current best config_002. This is the highest-value next step because: (1) it directly extends the strongest finding, (2) it cleanly isolates the aggregation choice, (3) the result will inform which aggregation to pair with multimodal fusion in later experiments, and (4) with 6 experiments left, establishing the best RNA-only baseline before moving to multimodal is the most budget-efficient path.

Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality (best RNA-only: 0.5907 vs image-only: 0.2079), and multiprofile+avgpool is the best-known profile/aggregation combination (0.5907 vs 0.5191 for transformer, 0.4849 for singleprofile). The current best uses a simple linear PCA encoder. Question: Does replacing PCA with a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) improve accuracy within the proven multiprofile+avgpool setup? This isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding profile and aggregation constant. Why this experiment: With 5 experiments remaining, the highest-expected-value move is to exploit the clearly superior multiprofile+avgpool RNA-only path and test whether a better encoder pushes accuracy above 0.59. If scvi_n200 helps, we can further refine; if not, we know the encoder is not the bottleneck and can pivot to testing scgpt or exploring whether multimodal fusion adds value on top of the best RNA configuration.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool is the strongest aggregation/profile setup and scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n200 by ~6 points. The key remaining uncertainty for the RNA-only track is whether scgpt, a fundamentally different learned encoder, can match or exceed scvi_n200. Question: config_008 (scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool) directly compares the scgpt encoder against scvi_n200 while holding profile setting and aggregation constant, isolating the encoder effect. Why this is the best next step: With 4 experiments left, I need to identify the strongest RNA-only baseline before investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion. If scgpt matches or beats scvi, it changes which encoder to pair with image modalities; if scvi remains superior, I can confidently proceed to multimodal configs with scvi_n200. This single comparison maximally reduces uncertainty about the encoder choice, which is the highest-leverage remaining design decision.

Evidence: RNA-only with scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool (config_005, 0.6501) is the clear best so far, and the RNA-only design space is well-mapped (avgpool > transformer, scvi > pca > scgpt, multi > single). Image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.208), but we have not tested a stronger image encoder. Uncertainty: whether a more powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) can provide complementary signal to the already-strong RNA representation. This experiment (config_036) tests the most logical multimodal extension: combining the best RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) with the strongest available image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) using simple concat fusion. It isolates the question 'does a strong image modality add value on top of the best RNA model?' with minimal confounding changes. With only 3 experiments remaining, this is the highest-upside test: if it beats 0.6501, we have a new best and can fine-tune fusion in the last 2 runs; if it does not, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and avoid wasting remaining budget on further image variants.

The current best is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy. The most direct and informative next step is to test config_037, which is identical except for using weighted fusion instead of concat. This isolates the single variable of fusion strategy while holding the proven-best encoder, image backbone, profile setting, and aggregation fixed. If weighted fusion improves on concat, it directly yields a new best; if not, it confirms concat is optimal for this architecture. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, a clean one-variable comparison against the current champion maximizes information gain and avoids wasting budget on less-supported directions (e.g., transformer aggregation or scgpt, both of which underperformed in RNA-only settings).

The current best is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, ViT-L, avgpool, concat) at 0.7150 acc. In RNA-only experiments, avgpool consistently outperformed transformer (0.5907 vs 0.5191 for PCA), but the multimodal setting introduces cross-modal interactions that could change this dynamic. Config_038 is the cleanest single-variable test against the best configuration—it changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping scvi_n200, ViT-L, multiprofile, and concat fusion fixed. This isolates whether transformer aggregation can better model multi-profile interactions when combined with image features. If it improves, we find a new best; if not, we confirm avgpool is optimal and reduce uncertainty for the final experiment. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the most direct extension of the current best is the highest-value use of the budget.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + ViT-L + multiprofile as the best model family (0.715–0.721 acc), with concat fusion and transformer aggregation as the top settings (config_038 at 0.721). Config_039 (transformer aggregation + weighted fusion) is the only remaining untested configuration in this top family, completing the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid. While prior evidence suggests concat > weighted (0.721 vs 0.706 for transformer; 0.715 vs 0.706 for avgpool), testing this final cell confirms whether the interaction between transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could yield an unexpected synergy. As the last experiment in the budget, this is the most targeted exploitation of the strongest evidence, ensuring no untested variant in the best-performing family is left unexplored. All other untested configurations involve inferior encoders (scgpt, PCA) or a much weaker image encoder (ResNet50, which scored only 0.208 image-only), making them very unlikely to surpass 0.721.

With no prior evidence, the highest-uncertainty question is establishing a reliable performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: a single modality, single profile, and the most standard/interpretable RNA encoder (PCA). This gives a clean reference accuracy without confounding from aggregation, fusion, or learned encoders. Establishing this floor is critical before investing experiments in more complex multimodal or multiprofile variants, because it tells us (a) whether RNA alone is competitive, (b) the pipeline is functioning correctly, and (c) how much headroom exists for improvements from image, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion. Under a 10-experiment budget, anchoring to the simplest baseline first maximizes the interpretability of all subsequent comparisons.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only ~48.5% accuracy, establishing a weak baseline. The most critical uncertainty at this stage is which modality (RNA vs. image) carries the most discriminative signal for this task, as this determines the entire branch of the config space to prioritize over the remaining 8 experiments. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) directly parallels config_001 with the modality swapped, isolating the effect of modality while holding profile setting and aggregation constant. Why: Resolving the modality question early is the highest-leverage decision—if image substantially outperforms RNA, I can focus remaining budget on image encoders and multimodal fusion; if RNA is stronger, I can invest in better RNA encoders (scgpt, scvi) and aggregation; if they are comparable, multimodal fusion becomes the key direction. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the dominant design axis with a clean, single-variable comparison.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is weak at 20.8%, confirming RNA is the dominant signal. The only RNA encoder tested so far is a linear method (PCA). Question: Does a learned nonlinear RNA representation (scvi_n200) improve over PCA n2000? This experiment (config_004) is a single-variable change from config_001—only the RNA encoder changes—so any accuracy shift can be cleanly attributed to the encoder. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether a better RNA representation can push accuracy above ~48% is the highest-leverage question before investing in multiprofile, image, or fusion experiments. If scvi_n200 helps, it justifies further RNA-side exploration (scgpt, multiprofile); if it doesn't, PCA is near-optimal and effort should shift to other axes.

Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality (0.48-0.52 vs 0.21 for image-only), and scvi_n200 (0.5203) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) by ~3.5%, showing that learned RNA representations matter. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested scgpt, the third available RNA encoder, and it may provide a substantially better or comparable representation. Question: config_007 (scgpt, singleprofile, rna_only) isolates the effect of the RNA encoder while holding profile setting and model setting constant, giving a clean three-way comparison (pca vs scvi vs scgpt). Why this is the best next experiment: Resolving which RNA encoder is strongest is the most fundamental design choice before investing the remaining 6 experiments in multiprofile or multimodal configurations. If scgpt is significantly better, all subsequent experiments should build on it; if it is comparable to or worse than scvi_n200, we confirm scvi as the backbone and can pivot to testing multiprofile or multimodal fusion in the next round. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty at minimal cost.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (0.5203 acc), clearly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.4849) and scgpt (0.4106), while image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.2079). We have no data on multiprofile yet. Question: Does multiprofile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool) improve on the singleprofile scvi_n200 baseline? This isolates the effect of the profile setting (single→multi) while keeping the encoder fixed at the best-performing one and using the least complex aggregation. Rationale: With 5 experiments remaining, confirming whether multiprofile adds value on the strongest RNA encoder is the highest-information next step. If avgpool helps, we can then test transformer aggregation (config_006) to see if more complex aggregation further helps. If it doesn't, we avoid wasting budget on transformer variants. This is a single-variable change from config_004, making it the cleanest comparison available.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over all singleprofile results, making it the clear current best. The only untested variable within this strong configuration is the aggregation method (transformer vs. avgpool). Question: Does transformer aggregation further improve over avgpool for the scvi_n200 multiprofile setup? Why this is the best next step: It is a single-variable change from the current best, cleanly isolating the aggregation effect. The answer directly informs whether to use transformer or avgpool in all remaining multimodal experiments (configs 030-039), making it the highest-information experiment before committing budget to multimodal fusion. With 4 experiments left, resolving this design choice now avoids wasting slots on a suboptimal aggregation in multimodal settings.

Evidence: RNA-only with scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer (config_006, 0.653) is the clear best so far, and multiprofile provides a ~13% boost over single profile. Image alone (resnet50) is very weak (0.208), so it's uncertain whether adding it provides any complementary signal. Question: Does fusing image (resnet50) via concat with the best RNA multiprofile model (scvi_n200, transformer) improve upon the 0.653 RNA-only baseline? This is the highest-value test because it directly probes whether multimodality can push past the current ceiling using the best-known components. Using concat (simpler) and resnet50 (the only image encoder with prior data) keeps the comparison clean. If multimodal helps, the remaining 3 experiments can explore weighted fusion and imagenet_vit_l; if it doesn't, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and conserve budget. This is the best use of experiment 7 because it tests the single most impactful unexplored direction (adding a second modality to the best RNA setup) with minimal confounding variables.

The current best (config_032, acc=0.6878) uses concat fusion in a multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer setup. The only untested axis in this exact configuration is the fusion strategy (weighted vs. concat). Since the image modality alone is weak (resnet50 singleprofile: 0.2079), a weighted fusion could allow the model to down-weight uninformative image features more effectively than a simple concatenation. This is a clean single-variable comparison to the current best, directly testing whether learned modality weighting improves over fixed concatenation. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, isolating the fusion effect is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step before exploring other axes (e.g., ViT-L image encoder) in the final experiments.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.7131. The strongest remaining uncertainty is whether a more powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) can further improve the multimodal pipeline. Image-only resnet50 was weak (0.208), yet it still contributed meaningfully in the multimodal setting (0.653→0.713), suggesting image quality matters. Config_039 changes exactly one variable from the current best—swapping resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l—while preserving all other winning settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of image representation quality. If it improves, we identify a new best with one experiment left for fine-tuning; if it doesn't, we confirm resnet50 is sufficient and can use the final experiment to probe another axis. This is the highest-information single experiment available under the remaining budget.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. Evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, multiprofile as essential, weighted fusion over concat (+0.025), and imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (+0.012). The only untested minor variant of this top configuration is swapping transformer aggregation for avgpool while keeping weighted fusion. In RNA-only, transformer vs avgpool made negligible difference (0.6530 vs 0.6501), but in the multimodal setting with a strong image encoder the interaction could differ slightly. Since this is the final experiment, config_037 is the safest exploitation of the current best: it preserves all top-performing components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion) and only tests the one remaining untested aggregation variant, giving the best chance of matching or marginally exceeding 0.7250 without risking a large drop from switching to concat fusion.

With no prior evidence, the highest-value first step is to establish a clean, minimal baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the search space: it uses a standard linear RNA representation (PCA-2000), a single profile, and no image modality. This gives a well-defined performance floor against which all other design choices (image modality, learned RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, fusion strategy) can be compared. Establishing this baseline first allows subsequent experiments to isolate the marginal contribution of each added component (e.g., adding image in config_010, then multimodal fusion in config_016), which is critical for making informed exploitation decisions within the 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: We have one data point (config_001, RNA-only/PCA/singleprofile at 48.5% accuracy), which establishes a low baseline but tells us nothing about the image modality's contribution. Uncertainty: The most critical open question for a multimodal profiling study is whether image features carry independent predictive signal for this task. This experiment tests: config_010 (image-only, singleprofile, ResNet50) provides a clean, single-modality anchor for the image side, directly comparable to the RNA-only baseline. Why this is the best next step: With 8 experiments remaining, establishing both single-modality baselines (RNA and image) before investing in multimodal fusion is the most information-efficient use of budget. It isolates the image encoder's contribution without confounding from fusion strategy, aggregation, or multiprofile effects, and will guide whether to prioritize image-based, RNA-based, or multimodal configurations in subsequent experiments.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, single profile, PCA n2000) achieved 48.5% accuracy, while config_010 (image-only, ResNet50) was very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. If scgpt matches or beats scvi_n200, it opens a new promising branch; if not, I can confidently build multimodal experiments on the scvi_n200 base.

Evidence: The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653. RNA is clearly dominant over image (0.65 vs 0.21 image-only resnet50), and scvi_n200 + multiprofile is the strongest RNA configuration. The key unresolved question is whether multimodal fusion can add complementary signal beyond the 0.653 RNA-only ceiling. This experiment tests the most promising multimodal extension: scvi_n200 (best RNA encoder), multiprofile (biggest single boost observed), transformer aggregation (marginally best), and imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder than the weak resnet50, which scored only 0.21 standalone) with concat fusion. If this cannot beat 0.653, multimodal is likely not fruitful and remaining budget should focus on RNA-only refinements. If it does, we have a new best to build on. This is the best use of experiment 7 because it directly tests the highest-leverage unexplored direction (can a better image encoder + fusion surpass the RNA-only ceiling?) while keeping all other components at their empirically best settings, isolating the multimodal contribution.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy, a strong jump over the best RNA-only (0.653). The evidence clearly shows: (1) scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder, (2) multiprofile is essential, (3) imagenet_vit_l is the strongest image encoder, and (4) multimodal fusion provides a substantial boost. The key remaining uncertainty within this winning configuration is the fusion method: concat (tested, 0.721) vs. weighted (untested). Config_039 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, isolating this single design choice. This is the cleanest and most informative next experiment: if weighted fusion improves accuracy, we gain a new best with 2 experiments left to confirm; if it does not, we confirm concat is optimal and can spend remaining budget on other refinements. With only 2 experiments remaining, this minimal-change comparison is the highest-value use of the next slot.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. All major design axes have been explored: multiprofile > singleprofile, scvi_n200 >> scgpt/pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l >> resnet50, weighted ≥ concat, and multimodal > RNA-only. The one remaining untested variation within the proven-best family is aggregation: in the RNA-only setting transformer (0.6530) marginally beat avgpool (0.6501), but in the multimodal setting the interaction between aggregation and fusion is untested. Config_037 changes only aggregation (transformer→avgpool) while keeping weighted fusion, multiprofile, scvi_n200, and imagenet_vit_l fixed. This isolates whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary in the multimodal context or whether avgpool performs comparably. With only one experiment remaining after this, confirming (or ruling out) a small improvement in the best-known architecture is the highest-value use of the budget, as no other untested configuration combines all the individually-validated best components.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. Three of the four aggregation×fusion combinations for this top encoder pair have been tested (transformer+weighted=0.725, transformer+concat=0.721, avgpool+weighted=0.706). Config_036 (avgpool+concat) is the only missing cell in this 2×2 grid. Running it completes the interaction picture, confirming whether transformer+weighted is robustly superior or whether the small gaps (0.004 for fusion, 0.019 for aggregation) are within noise. Since this is the final experiment and no untested configuration is likely to surpass config_039 (scgpt and pca_n2000 were substantially weaker in RNA-only; resnet50 was far weaker than imagenet_vit_l), the best use of the last slot is to lock in a complete, interpretable characterization of the best-performing model family rather than test a configuration with very low prior probability of improvement.

With no prior evidence, the priority is to establish a simple, interpretable baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal configuration in the search space: a single modality, single profile, and a standard linear (PCA) encoder. This gives a performance floor for RNA-only modeling and a reference point against which I can later assess whether learned encoders (scvi, scgpt), multiprofile aggregation, image modality, or multimodal fusion actually add value. Starting from the simplest configuration avoids conflating multiple design choices and ensures that any subsequent improvement can be attributed to a specific added component. With 9 experiments remaining, I can then systematically test image-only baselines, encoder comparisons, and multimodal fusion.

With only one completed experiment (RNA-only, PCA, single-profile at 48.5% accuracy), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality provides any discriminative signal at all. This question gates a large portion of the search space (36 of 51 configs are multimodal). Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest possible test: it mirrors the structure of the RNA-only baseline (single profile, standard pretrained encoder) while swapping only the modality. If image accuracy substantially exceeds or falls below the RNA baseline, it immediately informs whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing and which modality should anchor the best configuration. With 8 experiments remaining, resolving this fundamental modality question early is the highest-value use of the next slot, as it will guide whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion, stronger RNA encoders, or image encoder upgrades.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while Image (ResNet50, single profile) only reaches 0.208, indicating RNA is the dominant modality and the primary path to improvement. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can outperform the simple PCA baseline, or whether the 0.485 is near the ceiling for this modality. This experiment (config_004: RNA-only, single profile, scvi_n200) directly compares against config_001 by changing only the RNA encoder, isolating the effect of representation learning. If scvi_n200 improves accuracy, it justifies further investment in learned encoders and multiprofile variants; if it does not, PCA is sufficient and we should pivot to testing multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments remaining, this clean single-variable test is the most informative next step before committing budget to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: scVI n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (0.520 acc vs 0.485 for PCA), and image-only is weak (0.208), so RNA is the primary signal. The key remaining uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation adds value over the single-profile baseline. This experiment (config_005: scVI n200, multiprofile, avgpool) tests that question with the minimal change from the current best (config_004), isolating the effect of multiprofile + simple aggregation. If avgpool multiprofile improves on 0.520, it justifies further investment in transformer aggregation and multimodal variants; if it does not, we can deprioritize multiprofile and focus remaining budget on encoder choice (scGPT) or multimodal fusion. This is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step with 6 experiments left.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over singleprofile (0.520). The key uncertainty now is whether the aggregation method is a bottleneck: avgpool may be losing information that a transformer could capture. config_006 isolates exactly this variable (transformer vs avgpool) while holding encoder (scvi_n200) and profile setting (multiprofile) constant. This is the cleanest single-factor comparison to our current best, and the answer directly informs which aggregation to pair with any future multimodal or scgpt experiments. With 5 experiments remaining, establishing whether aggregation is a lever before adding more complexity (image, new encoders) is the highest-information next step.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy, showing that multiprofile + transformer aggregation is a strong combination. However, we have only tested scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting; scgpt remains untested there. Image alone was very weak (0.208), so before investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion, I want to confirm whether a different RNA encoder (scgpt) can outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile+transformer setting. This experiment isolates the encoder variable (scvi_n200 → scgpt) while holding profile_setting=multiprofile and aggregation=transformer constant, directly comparable to config_006. If scgpt improves, it gives a stronger base for subsequent multimodal experiments; if not, it confirms scvi_n200 is optimal and we can confidently pivot to multimodal fusion with scvi_n200 in the remaining 4 experiments.

The current best is RNA-only multiprofile scVI_n200 with transformer aggregation (config_006, acc 0.653). The most critical remaining question is whether adding image features via fusion can improve upon this strong RNA-only baseline, given that image-only was very weak (0.208). Config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_n200, ResNet50, transformer, concat) is a single-change extension of the best configuration—adding image via concat fusion while keeping all RNA-side settings identical. This isolates the effect of image fusion. If it helps, the 3 remaining experiments can refine (try ViT-L, weighted fusion, or avgpool); if it doesn't, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can focus remaining budget on minor RNA-only refinements. Testing this now, with 3 experiments left, is the highest-information use of experiment 7.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation as the core design, and adding the image modality via concat fusion yielded a ~3.5% gain over RNA-only. The most direct single-variable question to resolve is whether weighted fusion outperforms simple concat in this exact setting. Config_033 changes only the fusion method (concat → weighted), isolating that effect cleanly. This is the best use of experiment 8 because it directly exploits the strongest configuration with a minimal, interpretable modification, and the result will inform the final two experiments: if weighted wins, we can test it with ViT-L (config_039); if concat wins, we can test ViT-L with concat (config_038) to see if a stronger image encoder adds value.

The best result so far is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI, ResNet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 acc. The image modality clearly contributes meaningfully in fusion (RNA-only transformer at 0.653 → multimodal weighted at 0.713, a +0.06 gain), yet we have only tested ResNet50 as the image encoder, which performed very weakly in isolation (0.208). The key uncertainty is whether a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) can further improve the fused representation. Config_039 changes only the image encoder from ResNet50 to ViT-L while keeping all other proven-optimal settings (scVI, multiprofile, transformer, weighted), isolating the effect of image encoder quality. This is the highest-value experiment: if ViT-L helps, we find a new best; if not, we confirm ResNet50 is sufficient and retain config_033 as our answer. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, a clean single-variable test on the most impactful untested dimension is the best use of budget.

The current best (config_039, acc=0.7250) uses multimodal + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The only untested configuration that isolates a single variable from this best setup is config_038, which swaps weighted fusion for concat while keeping all other components identical. Evidence from config_032 vs config_033 (ResNet50) shows weighted > concat by ~2.5pp, but the ViT-L representation is substantially larger and may interact differently with the fusion strategy. As the final experiment, this completes the 2×2 fusion × image-encoder comparison at the known-optimal RNA/aggregation settings, confirming whether the weighted-fusion advantage holds with the stronger visual encoder or whether concat's simpler geometry might be competitive with ViT-L's richer features. It is the most informative single test remaining: it either confirms the current best is robust or reveals an unexpected fusion-image interaction that could shift the ranking.

With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is establishing a performance baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: a standard linear dimensionality reduction (PCA to 2000 dims) on a single RNA profile with no learned encoder, aggregation, or fusion. This isolates the raw signal in the RNA data without confounding from complex encoders or multimodal fusion. It answers the foundational question: 'How much accuracy is achievable from basic RNA features alone?' This floor is essential before interpreting whether learned encoders (scVI, scGPT), multiprofile aggregation, image modalities, or multimodal fusion add meaningful value. Choosing the simplest model first also minimizes the risk of training instability or hyperparameter sensitivity confounding the first data point. With 9 experiments remaining, this baseline enables a structured build-up: compare to image-only (config_010), then to better RNA encoders (config_004/007), then to multimodal (config_016), each step isolating one design dimension.

Evidence: We have only one data point (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), giving us a weak baseline with high uncertainty about every design axis. The largest open question is whether the image modality contributes meaningful signal at all, since it fundamentally determines whether we should invest remaining budget in multimodal configurations or focus on RNA encoder/profile variations. This experiment (config_016: multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the minimal extension of config_001—it keeps the same RNA encoder and profile setting and only adds the image branch with the simplest fusion (concat). This isolates the effect of adding image modality. If it substantially beats 48.5%, we gain strong evidence to exploit multimodal configurations in later experiments; if it does not, we can redirect budget toward RNA encoder and profile-setting comparisons. With 8 experiments remaining, resolving the modality question early is the highest-value use of the next slot.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, pca_n2000) achieved 0.485 acc, while config_016 (multimodal, pca_n2000 + resnet50, concat) achieved 0.527 acc, suggesting adding the image modality helps. However, we cannot yet tell how much of that gain comes from the image features themselves versus true cross-modal fusion. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the clean single-variable ablation of config_016 with RNA removed, directly measuring the image-only baseline. Why this is the best next experiment: establishing the image-only baseline is critical for interpreting all future multimodal results. If image-only is already ~0.50+, the multimodal gain is modest and we should prioritize other design axes (profile, encoder, fusion). If image-only is much lower (~0.35-0.40), fusion is genuinely powerful and we should invest remaining budget heavily in multimodal extensions. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most important design question (value of fusion) before committing 7 remaining experiments to a specific direction.

Evidence: Our current best is config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) at 0.527 acc, which modestly beats RNA-only (0.485) by ~4%. Image alone (resnet50) is very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality contributes limited signal with a standard CNN. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the image encoder is the bottleneck limiting the multimodal gain, or whether the image modality is fundamentally weak for this task. This experiment tests whether upgrading the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L (config_022) meaningfully improves the multimodal setup, while keeping all other settings identical to config_016 (pca_n2000, singleprofile, concat fusion). This is a clean single-variable comparison. If ViT-L yields a substantial improvement, it validates investing remaining budget in stronger multimodal variants (multiprofile, transformer aggregation). If it does not, it indicates the image modality is inherently limited here, and we should pivot remaining experiments toward improving the RNA representation (scgpt, scvi) or multiprofile aggregation in the RNA-only or multimodal setting.

All four completed experiments used singleprofile; the current best (config_022: multimodal, pca_n2000, vit_l, concat, acc=0.535) has not been tested with multiprofile. The single biggest unexplored design dimension is profile setting, and if multiprofile aggregation provides complementary information across profiles, it could yield a meaningful accuracy gain. config_024 is the most direct extension of config_022—changing only singleprofile→multiprofile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool)—so it cleanly isolates the multiprofile effect while keeping the proven RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion strategy fixed. If multiprofile helps, the remaining 5 experiments can explore transformer aggregation and weighted fusion; if it does not, we can redirect budget toward RNA encoder variants (scvi, scgpt) or fusion changes. This is the highest-information experiment available under the remaining budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile aggregation (config_024, acc=0.629) dramatically outperforms singleprofile multimodal (config_022, acc=0.535), a ~9.3% gain. The next logical step is to test whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer vs avgpool) can further improve on this best configuration. config_026 is identical to config_024 except aggregation changes from avgpool to transformer, cleanly isolating the effect of the aggregation method. This is the best use of experiment 6 because it directly exploits the strongest direction found so far while reducing uncertainty about whether avgpool is already capturing the relevant inter-profile structure or whether a learned attention-based aggregation (transformer) could extract additional signal. If it improves, we gain a new best; if not, we confirm avgpool suffices and can pivot to fusion or encoder choices in the remaining 3 experiments.

The current best is config_024 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.6287 acc. The multiprofile + ViT-L + avgpool combination showed a large gain over singleprofile (~9%), and avgpool clearly outperformed transformer (~3%). The remaining untested dimension within this proven configuration is the fusion strategy: concat vs. weighted. Config_025 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, keeping all other settings identical to the current best. This isolates the effect of learned fusion weights and directly tests whether we can push past 0.6287. With only 3 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest known configuration with a single clean variable change is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step before potentially exploring alternative RNA encoders in experiments 8–10.

The current best (config_025, acc=0.635) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion. All completed experiments have used pca_n2000, so the effect of a learned RNA representation remains entirely untested. Config_037 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to a learned scVI latent (200-dim), isolating the representation effect while holding all other settings at their known-best values. This is the highest-value single-variable test: if scVI captures nonlinear gene structure better than linear PCA, it could push accuracy above 0.635; if not, we confirm PCA is sufficient and can focus remaining budget on other axes. With only 2 experiments left, testing the most impactful unexplored dimension (RNA encoder quality) on the strongest backbone is the best use of this slot.

The strongest evidence from the search is that the RNA encoder is the most impactful design choice: switching from PCA to scvi_n200 in the multimodal/multiprofile/ViT-L/avgpool/weighted setting yielded a large jump from 0.635 to 0.706. The next logical question is whether another learned encoder (scgpt) can match or exceed scvi_n200 in this same setting. config_049 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt + imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates exactly this comparison while holding all other hyperparameters identical to the current best (config_037). This is the best use of experiment 9 because: (1) it directly tests the most important remaining uncertainty—whether a different learned RNA representation can further improve accuracy; (2) it changes only one variable relative to the best config, giving a clean comparison; and (3) with only one experiment remaining after this, testing the highest-leverage design axis (RNA encoder) in the proven best architecture maximizes the chance of finding a configuration that surpasses 0.706.

The current best is config_037 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) at 0.706 acc. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + weighted fusion. The one remaining uncertainty within this winning family is whether transformer aggregation could outperform avgpool specifically with the richer scvi_n200 latent representations (prior avgpool>transformer evidence was only with pca_n2000, a simpler linear projection). Config_039 changes only aggregation (avgpool→transformer) from the current best, cleanly isolating that effect. If transformer captures more complex cross-profile interactions in the learned latent space, it could push accuracy above 0.706; if not, it confirms avgpool is optimal and config_037 stands as the final best. This is the highest-value single-variable test for the last experiment.

With no prior experiments completed, there is zero evidence about which modality, encoder, profile setting, or fusion strategy is most effective. The highest-priority uncertainty is establishing a performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest, most standard configuration in the space: it uses a well-understood linear encoder (PCA-2000), avoids aggregation and fusion complexity, and isolates the RNA modality's contribution. This gives a clean reference accuracy against which all other design choices (image modality, learned encoders, multiprofile aggregation, multimodal fusion) can be evaluated in subsequent experiments. Starting with the simplest viable baseline is the most information-efficient first step under a tight 10-experiment budget, as it anchors the search and prevents misattributing performance gains to complexity rather than to a specific design choice.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the most critical uncertainty is which modality is most informative for this task. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides the cleanest single-variable comparison: same profile setting (single), same simplicity level (no aggregation/fusion), differing only in modality and encoder. This directly answers whether image features are competitive with or superior to RNA features, which is the foundational design decision that will determine whether to invest the remaining 8 experiments in RNA improvements, image improvements, or multimodal fusion. ResNet50 is also the image encoder used in the multimodal configs, so this result will inform multimodal expectations. Testing this early avoids wasting budget on multimodal or multiprofile variants before knowing which single modality carries signal.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 48.5% accuracy while image-only (ResNet50) is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether multiprofile aggregation improves RNA performance, which is a critical design axis that affects 6 of the 9 remaining RNA/multimodal configurations. This experiment (config_002) tests the single most important extension of our best result: changing from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder. It isolates the profile/aggregation effect with minimal variable change from config_001. If multiprofile helps, it justifies investing remaining budget in multiprofile variants; if not, we can focus on encoder quality (scvi, scgpt) instead. This is the highest-information experiment given 7 remaining slots.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) achieved 0.591 accuracy, a large jump over config_001 (RNA, single-profile, PCA) at 0.485, confirming multi-profile is strongly beneficial. Image (config_010, 0.208) is very weak. Uncertainty: whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) further improves over simple avgpool on the same multi-profile RNA setup. This experiment (config_003) isolates the aggregation variable by changing only avgpool→transformer while holding model_setting=rna_only, profile=multiprofile, and encoder=pca_n2000 constant. It is the best next step because it directly extends the current best result with a single-variable change, reducing uncertainty about the optimal aggregation strategy before committing budget to multimodal or alternative-encoder experiments. The outcome will inform aggregation choices for all subsequent multimodal configurations.

Evidence: RNA multi-profile with avgpool and PCA n2000 (config_002, acc=0.5907) is the clear best so far, outperforming single-profile (0.4849), transformer aggregation (0.5191), and image-only (0.2079). The only RNA encoder tested is PCA n2000. Uncertainty: whether a pre-trained single-cell foundation model (scgpt) can improve upon PCA in the proven best multi-profile + avgpool setup. This experiment (config_008) isolates the RNA encoder variable while holding profile=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool constant, enabling a clean comparison against config_002. It is the best next step because (1) RNA is the dominant modality, so optimizing its encoder is higher-value than testing multimodal fusion with a very weak image signal (0.21), (2) scgpt represents a fundamentally different representation type (pre-trained on large-scale scRNA-seq) versus PCA, so the information gain is high, and (3) the result directly informs which RNA encoder to pair with multimodal fusion in the remaining 5 experiments.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation is the strongest RNA configuration, and pca_n2000 outperforms scgpt. Image-only (resnet50) is very weak (0.208), but it is untested whether image features provide complementary signal when fused with the strong RNA representation. Question: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) directly extends config_002 by adding the image modality with the simplest fusion (concat), isolating the effect of multimodal fusion while keeping all other settings identical to the best RNA-only baseline. Why this experiment: With only 4 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information next step. If multimodal fusion improves on 0.591, we can then explore better image encoders (ViT-L) and fusion strategies (weighted) in the remaining budget. If it does not improve, we confirm RNA-only is sufficient and can focus remaining experiments on RNA encoder variants (e.g., scvi_n200) or accept the current best. This avoids changing multiple variables at once and gives a clean binary signal about whether the image modality is worth further investment.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc. The image-only model is very weak (0.208 acc), suggesting the image modality contributes limited signal and may be better handled by adaptive weighting rather than fixed concatenation. Config_019 is a clean single-variable comparison to config_018, changing only the fusion method from concat to weighted. This directly tests whether learned modality weighting can improve over naive concatenation, which is especially relevant given the large gap between RNA (0.591) and image (0.208) standalone performance. If weighted fusion helps, it confirms the fusion mechanism is a bottleneck; if not, it frees us to focus remaining budget on the image encoder (ViT-L) or RNA encoder choices. This is the highest-information, lowest-risk exploitation of the current best configuration with 3 experiments still remaining.

The current best (config_019, acc=0.639) uses multimodal + multiprofile + pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted. Evidence shows weighted>concat and avgpool>transformer, and that adding image to RNA helps (0.639 vs 0.591). However, the image-only model with resnet50 was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image encoder is a potential bottleneck in the multimodal fusion. Config_025 makes a single-variable change: upgrading the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other winning settings (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted). This directly tests whether a stronger, larger pretrained image representation can further improve the multimodal model. With only 2 experiments remaining, exploiting the best-known configuration with the most targeted upgrade is the highest-expected-value choice, and it cleanly isolates the image encoder effect.

The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.639 acc. Evidence consistently shows avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat, multiprofile > singleprofile, and multimodal > unimodal. The only major untested variable in the proven-best architecture is the RNA encoder: scvi_n200 has never been evaluated in any experiment. config_031 isolates this single change (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) while holding all other settings at their empirically best values. If scvi_n200 provides a richer or more discriminative RNA representation, this could push past 0.639; if not, it confirms pca_n2000 as optimal and we retain config_019 as our best. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve with one remaining experiment, as all other design axes (aggregation, fusion, profile, modality, image encoder) have already been tested and ranked.

The best result so far is config_031 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc 0.678). The scvi_n200 RNA encoder provided a substantial boost over pca_n2000 (0.678 vs 0.639), indicating learned representations matter. The image encoder comparison with pca_n2000 showed resnet50 ≈ imagenet_vit_l (0.639 vs 0.635), but that was with a linear PCA representation. With scvi_n200 (a learned, nonlinear encoder), the interaction with a more expressive image encoder (ViT-L) could differ, potentially capturing complementary spatial-structural features. Config_037 is a clean single-variable swap (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) from the current best, making it the most logical exploitation step. As the final experiment, it directly tests whether we can push past 0.678 by upgrading the image backbone while keeping all other proven-optimal settings (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion, scvi_n200) fixed.

With only 1 experiment remaining after this, a minimal-risk, targeted exploitation of the best-known configuration is the safest path to a potential small improvement, and it provides a clean comparison to confirm or reject whether fusion strategy matters in this regime.

The best result so far is config_033 (0.7131 acc) using multimodal/multiprofile/scVI_n200/ResNet50/transformer/weighted. The image modality adds ~6% over the best RNA-only model (0.6530), yet ResNet50 alone scored only 0.2079, suggesting the image encoder's representational quality is a bottleneck. Config_039 makes a single clean change—swapping ResNet50 for the stronger imagenet_vit_l—while keeping all other validated-optimal settings (scVI_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted fusion). This directly tests whether a more powerful image encoder can push the multimodal model beyond 0.7131. As the final experiment, exploiting the strongest identified direction with the highest-potential single upgrade is the best use of the last budget slot.

With no prior evidence, the highest-value first experiment is to establish the simplest possible baseline: RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-2000 (config_001). This gives a reference validation accuracy against which all subsequent complexity additions (multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders, image modality, multimodal fusion) can be measured. PCA is a cheap, well-understood encoder that avoids confounding the baseline with encoder-specific effects. Starting here lets me then isolate the marginal contribution of each design axis in subsequent experiments: (1) multiprofile+aggregation vs singleprofile, (2) image-only vs RNA-only, (3) multimodal fusion vs best single modality, and (4) encoder choice. Under a 10-experiment budget, anchoring to the simplest configuration first maximizes interpretability of every later comparison and avoids prematurely committing to a complex multimodal setup whose individual components are unvalidated.

We have only one data point (rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000 at ~48.5% accuracy), which is very low and gives us almost no information about which modality carries useful signal. The most critical uncertainty to resolve early is whether the image modality provides stronger or complementary signal compared to RNA. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest single-variable comparison to config_001: it swaps the modality while keeping profile setting (singleprofile) and encoder complexity (standard pretrained encoder) comparable. If image-only substantially outperforms RNA-only, we should prioritize image-centric or multimodal configurations in the remaining 8 experiments; if it is similarly poor, we know the bottleneck is representation quality rather than modality choice and should focus on stronger encoders (scgpt, ViT-L) or multiprofile aggregation. Resolving this modality question now prevents wasting budget on a suboptimal modality branch.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (single profile) achieved 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 was very weak at 20.8%, indicating RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether multiprofile aggregation can improve on the single-profile RNA baseline. This experiment (config_002) tests the minimal extension of the best result—changing only the profile setting from single to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder. It isolates the effect of multiprofile aggregation cleanly against config_001. If it improves accuracy, the next step would be to test transformer aggregation (config_003) or a stronger encoder; if it doesn't, we shift focus to encoder choice (scvi/scgpt). With 7 experiments remaining, this clean single-variable comparison is the highest-information next step before committing to more complex multimodal or encoder changes.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a large jump over config_001 (singleprofile, 0.485), confirming multiprofile aggregation is highly beneficial. Image-only is very weak (0.208), so RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: we don't yet know whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool for the multiprofile RNA setting. This experiment (config_003) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding rna_only, multiprofile, and pca_n2000 fixed, giving a clean single-variable comparison against the current best. If transformer helps, it establishes a stronger aggregation baseline before introducing new encoders or multimodal fusion; if it doesn't, avgpool is confirmed as sufficient and we can pivot to encoder exploration. With 6 experiments remaining after this, isolating the best aggregation for the proven multiprofile-RNA setup is the highest-information next step.

The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation is the strongest RNA setup and that avgpool beats transformer. However, we have only tested one RNA encoder (PCA, a linear method). The key uncertainty is whether a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) can further improve the multiprofile+avgpool pipeline. Config_005 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping the proven multiprofile+avgpool structure, isolating the representation-quality effect. This is the highest-value next experiment because RNA dominates over image (0.59 vs 0.21), so improving the RNA representation is the most direct path to higher accuracy, and a single-variable change from the best config gives the cleanest signal with 5 experiments remaining.

The current best is config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. The evidence shows avgpool > transformer for aggregation and scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 for encoding, but we have no data on whether scgpt outperforms scvi_n200 under identical conditions. config_008 (scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_005, isolating the encoder effect. This is critical because the encoder choice will determine the optimal multimodal configuration in the remaining 4 experiments; establishing the best RNA encoder now avoids wasting budget on suboptimal multimodal combinations. If scgpt wins, it opens a new exploitation path; if scvi_n200 holds, we can confidently build multimodal experiments on top of it.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is the best at 0.650 acc, and we know aggregation matters strongly for pca_n2000 (avgpool 0.591 >> transformer 0.519). Uncertainty: it is unclear whether the richer learned representations from scvi_n200 might interact differently with transformer aggregation than the linear pca_n2000 representations did. This experiment (config_006) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_005, isolating the aggregation choice while holding encoder (scvi_n200), profile (multiprofile), and modality (RNA) fixed. If transformer outperforms avgpool here, it opens a new optimization axis; if not, it confirms avgpool as the optimal aggregation for the best encoder, letting us allocate the remaining 3 experiments to testing whether multimodal fusion (with the best RNA backbone) can add incremental value over the 0.650 baseline.

Evidence: The best RNA-only result is config_006 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) at 0.653 acc / 0.628 F1, with config_005 (avgpool) nearly identical at 0.650. Image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), raising the question of whether adding image features to a strong RNA pipeline helps or hurts. Question: Does multimodal fusion (concat) of resnet50 image features with the best RNA pipeline (scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer) improve validation accuracy over the RNA-only baseline? This is the most direct, single-variable extension of our best result—adding only the image modality via concat fusion while keeping all other RNA-side choices identical to config_006. Why this is the best use of experiment 8: With only 2 experiments left, we need to determine whether the multimodal direction is worth pursuing at all. If concat fusion with resnet50 shows no gain (or a loss), we can rule out the simpler multimodal path and focus remaining budget on confirming the RNA-only optimum. If it shows a gain, the final experiment can test weighted fusion or ViT-L to squeeze out further improvement. This cleanly isolates the fusion effect without confounding with a new image encoder.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688. The image-only resnet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), raising the question of whether the image modality is inherently uninformative or simply poorly encoded by resnet50. Config_038 upgrades the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while holding all other settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, concat) at their best-known values, making it a clean single-variable comparison against config_032. If ViT-L improves the image representation, the multimodal fusion should benefit more and potentially surpass 0.688. This is the highest-impact remaining question: whether a stronger visual encoder unlocks additional signal in the multimodal setting. With only 1 experiment left after this, testing the most promising lever for improvement (image encoder quality) is the best use of the budget.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy. This is the cleanest exploitation experiment for the final budget slot: it isolates one design choice (fusion) on the strongest known base configuration, maximizing the chance of finding a new best without introducing confounding variable changes.

With no prior evidence, the highest-priority task is to establish a clean, minimal baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the space: it uses the most standard RNA encoder (PCA), avoids multiprofile aggregation complexity, and excludes image and fusion variables.
