With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries useful signal for this task. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides a clean modality comparison: it matches config_001 on profile setting (singleprofile) and uses a standard, well-established image encoder, isolating the effect of modality. If image_only substantially outperforms rna_only, the remaining budget should focus on multimodal or image-based configurations; if it underperforms, we can concentrate on RNA encoder improvements (scvi, scgpt) and profile settings. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the highest-leverage design choice before committing budget to more complex multimodal or multiprofile variants.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 48.5% accuracy while image (resnet50, singleprofile) only reaches 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The current RNA encoder is a simple linear PCA reduction, which may underrepresent the high-dimensional single-cell data. Question: Does replacing PCA with a learned deep generative encoder (scvi_n200) improve the RNA representation and thus validation accuracy? This experiment isolates the encoder effect by keeping profile_setting=singleprofile and aggregation=None identical to config_001, changing only the RNA encoder. Why this is the best next step: With 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether a learned encoder can beat PCA is the highest-leverage question for the RNA modality (the clearly stronger signal). A positive result would justify investing remaining budget in scvi-based multimodal configs; a null/negative result would confirm PCA is sufficient and redirect effort toward multiprofile or fusion strategies. This clean single-variable comparison maximizes information gained per experiment.

Evidence: RNA-only models dominate (0.48–0.52) over image-only (0.21), and scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (0.5203 vs 0.4849 for PCA). The multiprofile axis is completely unexplored across all three experiments. Question: Does aggregating multiple profiles (via avgpool) improve over the single-profile baseline, and does this benefit hold for the stronger scvi_n200 encoder? Why this experiment: config_005 is the minimal logical extension of the best result (config_004), changing only the profile setting from single to multi with the simplest aggregation (avgpool). This isolates the effect of multiprofile while using the best-known encoder, reducing uncertainty about whether profile diversity is a useful signal before investing remaining budget in more complex multimodal or transformer-aggregation variants.

The current best (config_005: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved 0.6501 accuracy, a large jump over singleprofile (0.5203). The most important open question is whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for multiprofile with the same scvi_n200 encoder. config_006 isolates exactly one variable (aggregation: transformer vs avgpool) while holding model setting, profile setting, and encoder constant. This single-variable comparison will determine whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based configurations (including multimodal) or to stick with avgpool. Given 5 experiments remain, establishing the optimal aggregation strategy early is critical for guiding all subsequent multimodal experiments.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.6530 accuracy. The multiprofile + transformer aggregation setup is clearly the strongest configuration family. The key remaining uncertainty within RNA is whether scgpt (a pretrained transformer-based encoder) can surpass scvi_n200 in this multiprofile setting. Config_009 isolates exactly this question by changing only the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while keeping the proven multiprofile + transformer aggregation. If scgpt improves, it gives a stronger backbone for subsequent multimodal experiments; if not, it confirms scvi_n200 as the best encoder and lets us confidently pivot to multimodal fusion with scvi_n200 in the remaining budget. This is a single-variable, high-information experiment that directly addresses the most impactful design choice (encoder) in the most promising setting.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.6530 accuracy. Image alone (resnet50) is very weak at 0.2079, and scgpt underperforms scvi_n200 in multiprofile settings. The critical open question is whether adding the image modality to the strongest RNA pipeline can improve upon 0.6530, or whether the weak image signal will only add noise. This experiment (config_032) directly extends the best-performing RNA configuration by adding resnet50 image features with concat fusion, keeping all other settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) identical. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion on the proven-best RNA setup. With 3 experiments remaining after this, confirming or ruling out the multimodal direction early is essential: if it helps, I can refine fusion strategy (weighted) or image encoder (ViT) in the last 3 slots; if it hurts, I can focus remaining budget on RNA-only refinements or alternative image encoders.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_200, ResNet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The evidence strongly supports this design space: multiprofile + scVI_200 + transformer aggregation is the best RNA backbone (0.653), and adding ResNet50 with concat fusion lifts it to 0.688. The only untested variable in this exact neighborhood is the fusion strategy. Config_033 is identical to config_032 except fusion changes from concat to weighted, cleanly isolating the effect of fusion. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, this is the highest-value exploitation step: if weighted fusion improves on 0.688, we secure a new best; if not, we confirm concat is optimal and can use the final 2 experiments to probe whether a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) or other refinement can push further. Changing only one variable keeps the comparison interpretable.

The current best (config_033, acc=0.713) uses scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted fusion + resnet50. The image-only resnet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), yet it still contributed meaningfully in the multimodal setting (0.713 vs 0.653 RNA-only). The most impactful untested variable is whether a stronger image encoder (ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L) can further boost the multimodal model. config_039 isolates exactly this: it swaps resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings at their empirically best values (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted). This is the single most informative next test because it directly extends the winning configuration along the one axis with the largest remaining uncertainty (image representation quality), and if it succeeds it sets a new best with one experiment still remaining for fine-tuning.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at acc=0.725. The evidence consistently shows weighted fusion > concat fusion (config_033 vs 032: 0.713 vs 0.688), scvi_n200 > scgpt/PCA, transformer ≥ avgpool, and ViT > resnet50. Config_038 is the only remaining untested configuration that shares every component with the current best except fusion method (concat instead of weighted). Testing it isolates whether there is any interaction between ViT's representation and concat fusion that could alter the fusion preference. While the prior evidence strongly favors weighted, this is the last experiment and the most informative remaining test: if concat with ViT somehow matches or exceeds 0.725, it reveals a useful interaction; if not, it confirms config_039 as the definitive best configuration with high confidence, closing the search cleanly.

With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a clean, minimal baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: one modality, one profile, a standard linear encoder, and no aggregation or fusion. This gives a well-defined reference accuracy for the RNA modality. Starting with the simplest baseline avoids confounding multiple design choices and provides the most interpretable anchor point for the 9 remaining experiments.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only 48.5% accuracy, suggesting the linear PCA representation may be a significant bottleneck. Question: Does a learned nonlinear RNA encoder (scvi_n200) substantially improve over PCA while holding all other factors constant (same model setting, profile setting, no image)? This controlled comparison maximizes information per experiment under the tight budget.

Evidence: config_004 (scvi_n200, singleprofile, RNA-only) achieved 0.5203 accuracy vs config_001 (pca_n2000) at 0.4849, suggesting a learned biological encoder is preferable. Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.520) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.485) in the simplest rna_only/singleprofile setting, and image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), confirming RNA as the dominant signal. Knowing the best RNA encoder before investing remaining budget in multiprofile aggregation, image modality, and multimodal fusion is critical: it ensures all downstream experiments build on the strongest single-modality baseline, avoiding wasted experiments on suboptimal encoders. Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (config_004: acc=0.520), and all tested models are singleprofile. If it does not help, we confirm avgpool is sufficient and can pivot to multimodal exploration with confidence.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. This is the highest-value experiment: if it beats 0.653, we have a new best and a direction to refine; if it doesn't, we confirm RNA-only multiprofile is the ceiling and can spend remaining budget on minor refinements.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 accuracy. This tests whether a more powerful image representation can further amplify the multimodal gain. The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. This is a single-variable comparison that directly tests whether concatenating the two modality representations preserves more discriminative information than the weighted combination. The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is which modality (RNA, image, or both) provides the strongest signal for this task. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible RNA baseline: it uses the most standard and computationally straightforward RNA encoder (PCA to 2000 dims) with a single profile, requiring no aggregation or fusion. Starting with the simplest configuration avoids confounding multiple design choices and maximizes the interpretability of the first data point under a tight 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: We have only one data point (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), which serves as a weak baseline. This isolates the effect of modality addition without confounding from encoder choice, aggregation, or fusion complexity. Evidence: RNA-only (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieved 0.485 accuracy, and adding ResNet50 image with concat fusion (multimodal) improved to 0.527. This +4.2 pt gain is meaningful but we cannot yet attribute it correctly—we don't know the image-only baseline. This single clean experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most important design axis before committing remaining budget to a specific direction.

Evidence: RNA-only with pca_n2000 (singleprofile) achieves 0.485 acc, and adding resnet50 via concat fusion yields a modest 0.527 acc (config_016), while image alone is very weak (0.208). This suggests RNA is the dominant signal and the image provides a small complementary boost. Key uncertainty: whether multiprofile (with avgpool aggregation) meaningfully improves the RNA representation beyond singleprofile. If multiprofile substantially lifts RNA accuracy, it justifies investing remaining budget in multiprofile multimodal configs (e.g., config_018/020); if it does not, we can focus on fusion strategy (config_017) or stronger image encoders (config_022). The strongest signal so far is that multiprofile RNA with avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) substantially outperforms singleprofile RNA (config_001, acc=0.485), and multimodal singleprofile with concat (config_016, acc=0.527) modestly beats rna_only singleprofile. The critical untested question is whether combining the multiprofile advantage with multimodal fusion (keeping the same concat strategy from config_016) can push accuracy beyond the current best of 0.591. config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the minimal, logical extension: it adds multiprofile to the already-tested multimodal+concat setup, isolating the effect of profile setting within the multimodal regime. This is the best use of experiment 5 because it directly tests the most promising unexplored combination; if it exceeds 0.591, we have a new best and can refine fusion/aggregation in remaining experiments, and if it does not, we gain strong evidence to focus remaining budget on rna_only multiprofile variants (e.g., transformer aggregation or alternative encoders).

The current best (config_018, acc=0.619) uses avgpool for multiprofile aggregation. The multiprofile setting has consistently provided large gains (+0.09–0.11 across modalities), suggesting the aggregation strategy is a critical design choice. Transformer aggregation (config_020) is a single-variable upgrade over avgpool that could capture inter-profile interactions missed by simple averaging, while keeping all other settings (pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) identical to the best config. This isolates the effect of aggregation method. With 4 experiments remaining after this, establishing whether transformer aggregation improves over avgpool is essential before investing in further changes (e.g., new encoders or fusion strategies), as it directly extends the strongest evidence and reduces uncertainty about the most impactful remaining design axis.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 accuracy. Evidence clearly shows multiprofile + avgpool + multimodal is the strongest combination, and transformer aggregation underperforms avgpool by ~4%. The key untested variable within this best configuration is the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted). config_019 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, providing a clean A/B comparison against config_018. Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 in single profile (config_001) achieved 0.485 accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) was very weak at 0.208, indicating RNA is the dominant signal and the current best baseline. This experiment (config_002) directly extends config_001 by switching from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder, cleanly isolating the effect of multiprofile aggregation. It is the best use of experiment 3 because it is the simplest logical extension of the current best result, provides a clear A/B comparison, and will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer aggregation, alternative encoders (scvi, scgpt), or multimodal fusion. With 7 experiments left, establishing whether multiprofile helps at all is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve before exploring more complex configurations.

Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality (0.485 vs 0.208 for image), and multiprofile with avgpool gave the largest single gain (0.485→0.591, +10.6 pts). Question: Does transformer aggregation further improve over avgpool for the multiprofile PCA-RNA pipeline? This tests exactly one variable (aggregation: transformer vs avgpool) against the current best (config_002), isolating the effect of aggregation strategy. Why this is the best next experiment: It is the most direct exploitation of the strongest evidence, requires only a single-variable change, and its result will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based configurations across encoders or to pivot toward testing alternative RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) with the simpler avgpool aggregation. With 6 experiments left, this clean comparison maximizes information per experiment.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation is the strongest RNA-only configuration, and PCA serves as a simple baseline encoder. Image-only is very weak (0.208), so RNA representation quality is the primary lever. Question: Does replacing PCA with a learned scVI encoder (scvi_n200) improve accuracy in the already-validated best profile/aggregation setting? This is a clean single-variable change from config_002, isolating the RNA encoder effect. Why this experiment: With 5 experiments remaining, establishing whether a learned encoder beats PCA in the best setting is critical for deciding whether to invest further budget in RNA encoder variants (scgpt) or pivot to multimodal fusion. If scvi_n200 helps, we have a clear exploitation path; if not, we confirm PCA suffices and can focus remaining budget on multimodal configurations.

The current best (config_005: scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, acc=0.650) establishes that multiprofile+avgpool is the strongest RNA-only combination, and scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n2000. The key remaining uncertainty for RNA-only is whether scgpt, a more powerful pretrained encoder, can further improve accuracy under the same multiprofile+avgpool setting. Config_008 isolates exactly this encoder effect (scgpt vs scvi_n200) while holding profile and aggregation constant, making it a clean single-variable comparison. With 4 experiments left, establishing the RNA-only ceiling is critical before deciding whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion (given image-only is very weak at 0.208, multimodal gains may be limited). This experiment maximizes information per trial by directly testing the most promising untested encoder in the proven best configuration.

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. The dominant finding is that RNA with scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool is the strongest single-modality configuration, and image-only (ResNet50) was very weak (0.208). The key remaining question is whether adding the image modality via fusion to the best RNA configuration can push accuracy above 0.650. Config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the minimal, logical extension of the best RNA setup: it keeps the proven multiprofile + scvi_n200 + avgpool settings and adds ResNet50 image features with the simplest fusion (concat). This isolates the effect of multimodal fusion without simultaneously changing aggregation or fusion strategy. If it improves, remaining budget can explore weighted fusion or ViT; if it doesn't, it confirms RNA-only is optimal and we can exploit further. This is the highest-information experiment under the 3-experiment remaining budget.

Evidence: The best result is config_005 (rna_only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. The best multimodal result, config_030 (same RNA/image/aggregation but concat fusion), scored 0.632—slightly below the RNA-only baseline, suggesting resnet50 image features may be adding noise under simple concatenation. Question: config_031 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, isolating whether learned modality weighting can mitigate the image's slight negative contribution and recover or exceed 0.650. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a minimal, clean A/B comparison (one variable changed vs config_030), directly tests whether the multimodal setup has untapped complementary signal, and the outcome cleanly determines the strategy for the final 2 experiments—if weighted fusion recovers to ≥0.650, remaining budget can explore ViT-L image encoders in multimodal; if it stays below, evidence strongly favors RNA-only and remaining experiments should target RNA-side improvements.

The current best is config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6776. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, multiprofile over singleprofile, avgpool over transformer (0.5907 vs 0.5191 for PCA), and weighted over concat fusion (0.6776 vs 0.6315). The one untested dimension that could plausibly push beyond 0.6776 is the image encoder: ResNet50 alone scored very poorly (0.2079), suggesting it may be a weak contributor even in fusion. config_037 swaps only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings identical to config_031 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted). This isolates the effect of image representation quality. If ViT-L provides a stronger visual signal, the weighted fusion should benefit more, potentially exceeding the current best. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, this single-variable exploitation of the most promising untested axis is the highest-expected-value choice.

The current best is config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.7062. The strongest evidence points to scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as the best image encoder, multiprofile as the best profile setting, and weighted as the best fusion. The one remaining unexplored dimension in this top configuration is aggregation: avgpool (tested, 0.7062) vs. transformer (untested). While RNA-only evidence favors avgpool over transformer (config_002: 0.5907 vs config_003: 0.5191), the multimodal context with a powerful ViT image encoder may change the dynamics—transformer aggregation could better model cross-profile and cross-modal interactions. As the final experiment, config_039 is the most direct logical extension of the current best, isolating the single variable (aggregation) that remains untested in the top-performing configuration, giving the best chance of either improving on 0.7062 or confirming avgpool as the optimal choice.

With no prior evidence, the highest-value first experiment is a simple, well-defined baseline to establish a performance reference. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal RNA configuration: a standard linear dimensionality reduction (PCA to 2000 dims), a single profile, and no aggregation or fusion complexity. This gives a clean floor for RNA-only performance and a direct comparison point for every other RNA-based variant (different encoders, multiprofile, aggregation). It is also the fastest configuration to train, preserving compute budget for the 9 remaining experiments. Establishing this baseline first lets subsequent experiments isolate whether image features, learned encoders (scvi, scgpt), multiprofile aggregation, or multimodal fusion actually add value over the simplest RNA signal.

The RNA-only PCA baseline (config_001) achieved only 48.5% accuracy, which is near chance level, indicating the current RNA representation is weak. The most critical uncertainty at this stage is whether the image modality carries useful predictive signal at all. Testing config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the modality question with a standard pretrained encoder and the simplest profile setting. If image-only accuracy substantially exceeds 48.5%, it validates the entire multimodal branch (configs 016-051) as a promising direction for the remaining 8 experiments. If it is also poor, we should pivot to testing stronger RNA encoders (scvi_n200, scgpt) to find where the signal lives. This single-variable comparison (modality swap, same profile setting) is the highest-information experiment to resolve before committing budget to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieved 0.485 accuracy, far outperforming image-only ResNet50 (0.208), establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the multiprofile setting (capturing multiple cell profiles per sample with aggregation) can further improve the RNA signal beyond the single-profile baseline. This experiment (config_002) tests that single conceptual change—multiprofile with avgpool aggregation—while keeping the same PCA n2000 encoder and RNA-only model, giving a clean comparison against config_001. It is the best use of experiment 3 because it directly extends our strongest configuration with a minimal, interpretable modification; if multiprofile+avgpool helps, we can then explore transformer aggregation (config_003) or combine multiprofile with learned encoders (scvi, scgpt) in later experiments. If it doesn't help, we learn that the single-profile PCA representation is already near its ceiling and should pivot to testing better encoders (config_004/007) or a stronger image encoder (config_013) to inform whether multimodal fusion is worthwhile.

Evidence: config_002 (multiprofile, PCA, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a large jump over config_001 (singleprofile, PCA) at 0.485, confirming that multiprofile aggregation is highly beneficial. Image-only (config_010) is very weak (0.208), so RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether transformer aggregation outperforms simple avgpool for combining multiple profiles. This experiment (config_003) isolates exactly that question by changing only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and pca_n2000 fixed. It is the best use of experiment 4 because it directly extends the strongest result so far with a single-variable change, establishing the best RNA-only baseline before spending remaining budget on encoder swaps (scvi/scgpt) or multimodal fusion, which carry higher risk given the weak image signal.

The best result so far is config_002 (RNA-only, multi-profile, PCA n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 accuracy, and multi-profile + avgpool is clearly the strongest aggregation strategy (0.591 vs 0.519 for transformer). The key unexplored dimension is the RNA encoder: PCA is a linear method, while scvi_n200 is a learned non-linear encoder that may capture richer single-cell structure. Config_005 (scvi_n200, multi-profile, avgpool) isolates the encoder effect by changing only the RNA encoder relative to config_002, making it a clean A/B comparison. Since image-only performance is very weak (0.208), improving the RNA signal is the most direct path to higher accuracy. With 5 experiments remaining, establishing whether a learned encoder beats PCA in the best-known setting is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve before investing in multimodal fusion experiments.

Evidence: The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. We know multiprofile+avgpool is the best profile/aggregation combo, and scvi_n200 outperformed pca_n2000. The key remaining uncertainty is whether scgpt, the third available RNA encoder, could surpass scvi_n200 in this optimal setup. This experiment (config_008: rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) isolates the encoder variable while holding profile and aggregation at their proven-best settings, giving a clean head-to-head comparison against config_005. It is the best use of this slot because: (1) it directly tests the most impactful remaining design choice (RNA encoder quality), (2) it avoids the low-probability direction of transformer aggregation (already shown inferior to avgpool), and (3) it avoids multimodal fusion where image alone is very weak (0.208), making a positive fusion effect unlikely. With 4 experiments left, confirming the best encoder now lets subsequent experiments build on the strongest foundation.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy. We know avgpool outperformed transformer for pca_n2000 (0.591 vs 0.519), and scvi_n200 outperformed both pca_n2000 and scgpt under avgpool. However, we have not tested whether the aggregation preference (avgpool > transformer) is encoder-dependent—scvi_n200 produces a learned latent representation that may interact differently with transformer attention than with simple averaging. This experiment (config_006) is a single-variable change from config_005 (avgpool → transformer), cleanly isolating the aggregation effect under the best encoder. If it beats 0.650, we find a new best; if not, we confirm avgpool is optimal for scvi_n200 and can confidently direct the remaining 3 experiments toward testing whether multimodal fusion (with a stronger ViT-L image encoder) can add value on top of the best RNA-only setup, rather than wasting budget on suboptimal aggregation choices.

The best result so far is config_006 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy, with config_005 (avgpool) very close at 0.650. Image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), but no multimodal configuration has been tested yet. The critical remaining question is whether adding image features to the strongest RNA setup can push past 0.653. Config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) directly extends the best RNA-only configuration by adding image via the simplest fusion mechanism (concat), isolating the effect of modality addition. If it improves, I have one experiment left to try weighted fusion or ViT-L; if it does not, I confirm RNA-only is optimal and can use the final experiment to verify or explore a small variant. This is the highest-information experiment for the remaining budget.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688. The image modality is very weak standalone (0.208 with resnet50), yet it still contributes ~3.5% when concatenated with the strong RNA signal. This raises the question of whether a weighted fusion—allowing the model to learn modality-specific importance—can outperform simple concatenation by downweighting the weaker image features. Config_033 changes only the fusion method (concat→weighted) while keeping all other settings identical to config_032, making it a clean, single-variable comparison. This is the best use of experiment 9 because it directly exploits the strongest result with a minimal, well-motivated modification; if it improves on 0.688, we secure a better final answer, and if it does not, we retain one experiment to explore the image-encoder axis (e.g., ViT-L via config_038).

The best result so far is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, ResNet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.7131 accuracy. Evidence consistently shows scvi_n200 > scgpt > PCA, multiprofile > singleprofile, transformer ≥ avgpool, and weighted > concat. The primary remaining uncertainty is the image encoder: ResNet50 is a relatively modest backbone, while imagenet_vit_l (ViT-Large) is a substantially stronger visual encoder. Config_039 is a clean single-variable extension of config_033, swapping only ResNet50 → imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other components (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) fixed at their empirically best settings. As the final experiment in the budget, exploiting the strongest identified direction with the highest-impact untested variable (image encoder capacity) is the best use of the last slot, and a stronger visual representation could plausibly push accuracy above 0.7131.
